  29class BrachyDose:
  30    r"""
  31    Purpse:
  32        - This class holds information regarding a dose and uncertainty distribution as well as the fundamental
  33    functions that are applied on the dose. All doses are expressed in Gy and all the unit length is mm.
  34
  35    Attributes:
  36        - dose_image:DoseImage := DoseImage object holding the dose grid ([x, y, z]), as well as
  37            spacing, origin, and rotation ([x, y, z]) information.
  38        - uncertainty_image:DoseImage := DoseImage object holding the dose uncertainity grid ([x, y, z]), as well as
  39            spacing, origin, and rotation ([x, y, z]) information.
  40        - voxel_edges:np.ndarray := coorindates of voxel edges along x, y and z axis.
  41        - interpolation_function := RegularGridInterpolator object that allows for sampling of dose at arbitrary points ([x, y, z]).
  42    Functions:
  43        - load_file_to_brachydose
  44        - write_brachydose_to_file
  45        - load_from_3ddose
  46        - load_from_nrrd
  47        - load_from_npz
  48        - load_from_dicom
  49        - load_from_minidos
  50        - create_interpolation_function
  51        - extract_dose_values_from_coordinates
  52        - extract_profile_2d
  53        - extract_profile_1d
  54        - get_average_uncert
  55        - get_average_uncert_benchmark
  56        - pad_3ddose
  57        - write_to_3ddose
  58        - write_to_nrrd
  59        - write_to_npz
  60        - write_to_minidos
  61        - crop_by_coordinates
  62        - crop_by_index
  63        - crop_by_fraction
  64
  65    Dependencies:
  66        - opentps.core
  67        - matplotlib
  68        - scipy
  69        - pymedphys
  70        - SimpleITK
  71    """
  72
  73    def __init__(
  74        self,
  75        pth_dose_file: Optional[Path] | tuple[np.ndarray, defaultdict] = None,
  76        load_uncertainty: Optional[bool] = True,
  77        dtype=np.float32
  78    ):
  79        self.path = Path(pth_dose_file) if pth_dose_file else None
  80        self.dose_image: DoseImage = None
  81        self.uncertainty_image: DoseImage = None
  82        self.voxel_edges: np.ndarray = None
  83        self.interpolation_function = None
  84        if pth_dose_file is not None:
  85            self.load_file_to_brachydose(pth_dose_file, load_uncertainty)
  86        if self.dose_image is not None:
  87            self.create_interpolation_function()
  88        # default dose unit length is mm
  89        self.unit_length: Literal["mm"] = "mm"
  90        self.xyz_format: bool = True
  91        self.modification_time:float = self.path.stat().st_mtime if self.path else None
  92        if self.dose_image is not None:
  93            self.dose_image.imageArray = self.dose_image.imageArray.astype(dtype)
  94        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
  95            self.uncertainty_image.imageArray = self.uncertainty_image.imageArray.astype(dtype)
  96
  97    def load_file_to_brachydose(
  98        self, pth_dose_file: Path, load_uncertainty: Optional[bool] = True,
  99    ) -> None:
 100        r"""
 101        Purpose:
 102            - given the path to a file holding dose information, it will return
 103        a BrachyDose object with the populated available attributes.
 104
 105        Inputs:
 106            - pth_dose_file := path directory where the file containing the dose is. The file
 107                extension could be ".3ddose", ".nrrd", ".dcm", or ".minidos"
 108            - load_uncertainty := a boolean flag to load the uncertainty image if it is available.
 109        Output:
 110            - None := the contents of the file are loaded into the BrachyDose object.
 111        Dependencies:
 112            - load_from_3ddose()
 113            - load_from_nrrd()
 114            - load_from_dicom()
 115            - create_interpolation_function()
 116        """
 117        if isinstance(pth_dose_file, tuple):
 118            assert len(pth_dose_file) == 2, "If a tuple is provided, it must be of length 2"
 119            assert isinstance(pth_dose_file[0], np.ndarray), "First element of the tuple must be a numpy array"
 120            assert isinstance(pth_dose_file[1], defaultdict), "Second element of the tuple must be a dictionary"
 121            self.load_from_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
 122        else:
 123            pth_dose_file = os.path.abspath(pth_dose_file)
 124
 125            file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
 126
 127            if file_extension == ".3ddose":
 128                self.load_from_3ddose(pth_dose_file, load_uncertainty)
 129            elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
 130                self.load_from_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
 131            elif file_extension == ".dcm":
 132                self.load_from_dicom(pth_dose_file)
 133            elif file_extension == ".gz" or file_extension == ".nii":
 134                self.load_from_nifti(pth_dose_file)
 135            elif file_extension == ".minidos":
 136                raise NotImplementedError(
 137                    "loading dose from .minidos file is not currently supported"
 138                )
 139            elif file_extension == ".bindose":
 140                raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
 141            else:
 142                raise ValueError("file extension not recognized")
 143            if self.dose_image is None:
 144                raise ValueError("dose image not loaded")
 145        if self.interpolation_function is None and self.dose_image is not None:
 146            self.create_interpolation_function()
 147
 148    def write_brachydose_to_file(self, pth_dose_file: Path | str) -> None:
 149        r"""
 150        Purpose:
 151            - To write a brachy dose object to the given file path. this function will automatically
 152        detect the type of the output file and will call the right brachyDose writer function.
 153        Inputs:
 154            - pth_dose_file := path where the BrachyDose contents will be written to. The options
 155            for output type are "3ddose", "nrrd", "npz", "minidos", "xz", and "zstd".
 156        Dependencies:
 157            - write_to_3ddose()
 158            - write_to_nrrd()
 159            - write_to_npz()
 160            - write_to_minidos()
 161            - write_to_xz()
 162            - write_to_zstd()
 163        Output:
 164            - None := contents of self is written to "pth_dose_file"
 165        """
 166        pth_dose_file = Path(pth_dose_file)
 167        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
 168        pth_dose_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 169        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
 170            self.write_to_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
 171
 172        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
 173            self.write_to_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
 174
 175        elif file_extension == ".dcm":
 176            self.write_to_dicom(pth_dose_file)
 177
 178        elif file_extension == ".npz":
 179            self.write_to_npz(pth_dose_file)
 180
 181        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
 182            self.write_to_minidos(pth_dose_file)
 183
 184        elif file_extension == ".xz":
 185            self.write_to_xz(pth_dose_file)
 186
 187        elif file_extension == ".zstd":
 188            self.write_to_zstd(pth_dose_file)
 189
 190        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
 191            raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
 192        else:
 193            raise ValueError(
 194                f"The input file name {pth_dose_file} is not supported. the supported \
 195            file types are '.3ddose', '.nrrd', '.npz', '.minidos', '.xz', and '.zstd'"
 196            )
 197
 198    def load_from_3ddose(
 199        self, filename: Path, load_uncertainty: Optional[bool] = True
 200    ) -> None:
 201        r"""
 202        Purpose:
 203            - Given the path to a 3ddose file, load its content into self:BrachyDose.
 204        Input:
 205            - filename := path to a ".3ddose" file
 206        Outputs:
 207            - void := contents of self is updated.
 208        Dependencies:
 209            - numpy
 210            - os
 211        """
 212        assert (
 213            os.path.splitext(filename)[-1] == ".3ddose"
 214        ), "this file should have '3ddose' extension."
 215        path = filename
 216        # print("Opening 3ddose at %s" % path)
 217        with open(path, "rb") as newfile:
 218            bench_voxels = [int(i) for i in newfile.readline().split()]
 219            bench_x_pos = (
 220                np.round(
 221                    np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6
 222                )
 223                * 10
 224            )
 225            bench_y_pos = (
 226                np.round(
 227                    np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6
 228                )
 229                * 10
 230            )
 231            bench_z_pos = (
 232                np.round(
 233                    np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6
 234                )
 235                * 10
 236            )
 237
 238            bench_spacing = np.array(
 239                [
 240                    bench_x_pos[1] - bench_x_pos[0],
 241                    bench_y_pos[1] - bench_y_pos[0],
 242                    bench_z_pos[1] - bench_z_pos[0],
 243                ]
 244            )
 245            bench_origin = np.array(
 246                [
 247                    bench_x_pos[0] + bench_spacing[0] / 2,
 248                    bench_y_pos[0] + bench_spacing[1] / 2,
 249                    bench_z_pos[0] + bench_spacing[2] / 2,
 250                ],
 251                dtype=np.float32,
 252            )
 253
 254            huge_dose_array = np.array(
 255                newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32
 256            )
 257            try:
 258                bench_dose = reshape(
 259                    huge_dose_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0])
 260                )
 261            except ValueError as e:
 262                print(f"Error in dose file {filename}: {e}", "\n")
 263                bench_dose = None
 264
 265            if load_uncertainty:
 266                try:
 267                    huge_uncert_array = np.array(
 268                        newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32
 269                    )
 270                    bench_uncert = reshape(
 271                        huge_uncert_array,
 272                        (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]),
 273                    )
 274                    self.uncertainty_image = DoseImage(
 275                        # convert numpy zyx to xyz in opentps.
 276                        imageArray=np.swapaxes(bench_uncert, 0, 2),
 277                        origin=bench_origin,
 278                        spacing=bench_spacing,
 279                    )
 280                except ValueError:
 281                    print("Warning: No uncertainty in the 3ddose file", filename, "\n")
 282
 283            self.dose_image = DoseImage(
 284                # convert numpy zyx to xyz in opentps.
 285                imageArray=np.swapaxes(bench_dose, 0, 2),
 286                origin=bench_origin,
 287                spacing=bench_spacing,
 288            )
 289            self.voxel_edges = self.get_voxel_edges()
 290
 291    def load_from_nrrd(self, pth_nrrd: Path|tuple[np.ndarray, defaultdict]) -> None:
 292        r"""
 293        Purpose:
 294            - given the path to a .nrrd dose file, it will load its content into self:BrachyDose
 295        Inputs:
 296            - pth_nrrd := Path to a .nrrd file writtern. by default, we assume c index ordering is done.
 297        Outputs:
 298            - void := contents of self is updated.
 299        Dependencies:
 300            - nrrd
 301            - get_voxel_edges()
 302        """
 303        # nrrd.reader._READ_CHUNKSIZE = 500 * 1024 * 1024  # 500MB
 304        if isinstance(pth_nrrd, tuple):
 305            dose_uncertainty, header = pth_nrrd
 306        else:
 307            dose_uncertainty, header = nrrd.read(pth_nrrd, index_order="C")
 308
 309        if dose_uncertainty.shape[0] == 2:
 310            dose_array = dose_uncertainty[0]
 311            uncertainty_array = dose_uncertainty[1]
 312        elif dose_uncertainty.shape[-1] == 2:
 313            dose_array = dose_uncertainty[:, :, :, 0]
 314            uncertainty_array = dose_uncertainty[:, :, :, 1]
 315            affine = header.get("space directions")[1:]
 316        else:
 317            # print("Uncertainty not found in the nrrd file")
 318            dose_array = dose_uncertainty
 319            uncertainty_array = None
 320            affine = header.get("space directions")
 321
 322        voxel_size = affine.diagonal()
 323        origin_coordinates = np.array(header.get("space origin")).astype(np.float32)
 324        orientation = header.get("space").split("-")
 325        orientation = "".join([char[0].upper() for char in orientation])
 326        self.dose_image = DoseImage(
 327            # imageArray=np.swapaxes(dose_array, 0, 2),
 328            origin=origin_coordinates,
 329            spacing=voxel_size,
 330        )
 331        self.set_dose_array(dose_array)
 332        self.uncertainty_image = (
 333            DoseImage(
 334                # imageArray=np.swapaxes(uncertainty_array, 0, 2),
 335                origin=origin_coordinates,
 336                spacing=voxel_size,
 337            )
 338            if uncertainty_array is not None
 339            else None
 340        )
 341        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
 342            self.set_uncertainty_array(uncertainty_array)
 343        self.dose_image.to_lps(current_orientation=orientation)
 344        self.voxel_edges = self.get_voxel_edges()
 345
 346    def load_from_npz(self, pth_npz: Path) -> None:
 347        r"""
 348        Purpose:
 349            - Given the path to an npz file, load its content into self:BrachyDose.
 350        Input:
 351            - filename := path to a ".npz" file
 352        Outputs:
 353            - void := contents of self is updated.
 354        Dependencies:
 355            - numpy
 356        """
 357
 358        assert (
 359            os.path.splitext(pth_npz)[-1] == ".npz"
 360        ), "the file extension should be npz"
 361
 362        loaded_brachydose = np.load(pth_npz, allow_pickle=True)
 363        self.dose_image = loaded_brachydose.get("dose_image")
 364        self.uncertainty_image = loaded_brachydose.get("uncertainty_image", None)
 365        self.get_voxel_edges()
 366        self.create_interpolation_function()
 367
 368    def load_from_dicom(self, pth_RD_dicom: Path):
 369        r"""
 370        Purpose:
 371            - Given the path to a dicom dose file, load its content into self:BrachyDose.
 372        Inputs:
 373            - pth_RD_dicom := path to a dicom dose file. baseename must start with "RD".
 374        Outputs:
 375            - void := contents of self is updated.
 376        Dependencies:
 377            - pydicom
 378        """
 379        from opentps.core.io.dicomIO import readDicomDose
 380
 381        assert os.path.basename(pth_RD_dicom).startswith(
 382            "RD"
 383        ), "the basename should start with RD"
 384        self.dose_image = readDicomDose(pth_RD_dicom)
 385        if self.dose_image is None:
 386            warnings.warn("No dose image found in the dicom file", stacklevel=2)
 387            return
 388        if self.dose_image.spacing[2] == 0:
 389            if self.dose_image.spacing[0] == self.dose_image.spacing[1]:
 390                self.dose_image.spacing[2] = self.dose_image.spacing[0]
 391            else:
 392                self.dose_image.spacing[2] = 1.0
 393                warnings.warn(
 394                    "The z spacing is not defined in the dicom file and the x and y spacing are not the same. Z spacing is set to 1mm.",
 395                    stacklevel=2,
 396                )
 397
 398        self.voxel_edges = self.get_voxel_edges()
 399
 400    def load_from_nifti(self, pth_nifti: Path):
 401        pth_nifti = Path(pth_nifti)
 402        import nibabel as nib
 403        dose_nifti = nib.load(str(pth_nifti))
 404        orientation = "".join(nib.aff2axcodes(dose_nifti.affine))
 405        dose_data = np.ascontiguousarray(dose_nifti.get_fdata())
 406        origin = dose_nifti.affine[:3, 3]
 407        spacing = dose_nifti.header.get("pixdim")[1:4]
 408        origin = np.array([
 409            origin[0] * np.sign(dose_nifti.affine[0][0]),
 410            origin[1] * np.sign(dose_nifti.affine[1][1]),
 411            origin[2] * np.sign(dose_nifti.affine[2][2]),
 412        ])
 413        self.dose_image = DoseImage(
 414            imageArray=dose_data,
 415            origin=origin,
 416            spacing=spacing,
 417        )
 418        self.dose_image.to_lps(current_orientation=orientation)
 419        # self.voxel_edges = self.get_voxel_edges()
 420

 437    def create_interpolation_function(self) -> None:
 438        r"""
 439        Purpose:
 440            - To create an interpolation function for the dose grid.
 441            it allows for sampling of dose at any arbitrary set of points.
 442        Inputs:
 443            - self:BrachyDose := the object must have the grid attribute populated.
 444        Outputs:
 445            - void := the interpolation function is stored in the object.
 446        Dependencies:
 447            - scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator()
 448        """
 449        voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
 450        self.interpolation_function = RegularGridInterpolator(
 451            (voxel_centers[0], voxel_centers[1], voxel_centers[2]),
 452            self.dose_image.imageArray,
 453            bounds_error=False,
 454            fill_value=0,
 455        )
 456
 457    def extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(self, x, y, z, uncertainty = False):
 458        # r""" """
 459        # raise DeprecationWarning(
 460        #    "This function is no longer supported due to migration to open tps. please use self.get_dose_at_coordinates() instead."
 461        # )
 462        # self.is_not_empty()
 463        # if self.interpolation_function is None:
 464        #    raise ValueError("interpolation function is not defined")
 465        shape = []
 466        axis = []
 467        for coord in [z, y, x]:
 468            if isinstance(coord, float):
 469                coord_size = 1
 470                axis.append([coord])
 471            elif isinstance(coord, np.ndarray):
 472                coord_size = coord.size
 473                axis.append(coord)
 474            else:
 475                raise TypeError("x, y, and z should be either floats or numpy arrays")
 476            shape.append(coord_size)
 477        coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x = np.meshgrid(
 478            [z], [y], [x], indexing="ij"
 479        )
 480        if not uncertainty:
 481        # trunk-ignore(ruff/E731)
 482            dose_grid_lambda = lambda xs, ys, zs: self.dose_image.getDataAtPosition(
 483                (xs, ys, zs)
 484            )
 485            dose_grid_function = np.vectorize(dose_grid_lambda)
 486            dose_grid = dose_grid_function(coord_grid_x, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_z)
 487            dose_grid.reshape(shape)
 488            return dose_grid.squeeze()
 489        else:
 490            uncertainty_grid_lambda = lambda xs, ys, zs: self.uncertainty_image.getDataAtPosition(
 491                (xs, ys, zs)
 492            )
 493            uncertainty_grid_function = np.vectorize(uncertainty_grid_lambda)
 494            uncertainty_grid = uncertainty_grid_function(coord_grid_x, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_z)
 495            uncertainty_grid.reshape(shape)
 496            return uncertainty_grid.squeeze()
 497
 498    def extract_profile_2d(
 499        self,
 500        axis_1_coords: np.ndarray,
 501        axis_2_coords: np.ndarray,
 502        plane_coord: float,
 503        plane: str,
 504    ):
 505        if (
 506            not isinstance(axis_1_coords, np.ndarray)
 507            or not isinstance(axis_2_coords, np.ndarray)
 508            or not isinstance(plane_coord, float)
 509        ):
 510            raise TypeError(
 511                "axis_1_coords and axis_2_coords should be numpy arrays and plane_coord should be a float"
 512            )
 513        if plane == "xy":
 514            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
 515                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord
 516            )
 517        elif plane == "xz":
 518            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
 519                axis_1_coords, plane_coord, axis_2_coords
 520            )
 521        elif plane == "yz":
 522            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
 523                plane_coord, axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords
 524            )
 525        elif plane == "yx":
 526            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
 527                axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, plane_coord
 528            )
 529        elif plane == "zx":
 530            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
 531                axis_2_coords, plane_coord, axis_1_coords
 532            )
 533        elif plane == "zy":
 534            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
 535                plane_coord, axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords
 536            )
 537        else:
 538            raise ValueError(
 539                "plane should be one of the following: 'xy', 'xz', 'yz', 'yx', 'zx', 'zy'"
 540            )
 541
 542    def extract_profile_1d(
 543        self,
 544        axis: str,
 545        axis_1_coords: np.ndarray,
 546        axis_2_coords: np.ndarray,
 547        axis_3_coords: List[float],
 548    ) -> np.ndarray:
 549        r"""
 550        Extracts a 1D line profile from the dose grid along the specified axis, given the coordinates of the other two axes and a list of coordinates along the axis of extraction.
 551
 552        Parameters:
 553            - axis (str): the axis along which to extract the line profile. Must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'.
 554            - axis_1_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the first axis, as a 1D numpy array.
 555            - axis_2_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the second axis, as a 1D numpy array.
 556            - axis_3_coords (List[float]): the coordinates along the axis of extraction, as a list of floats.
 557
 558        Returns:
 559            - profile (np.ndarray): the line profile extracted from the dose grid, as a 1D numpy array.
 560        """
 561        if axis not in ["x", "y", "z"]:
 562            raise ValueError("axis must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'")
 563
 564        if axis == "x":
 565            x = np.array(axis_3_coords)
 566            y, z = np.meshgrid(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, indexing="ij")
 567        elif axis == "y":
 568            y = np.array(axis_3_coords)
 569            x, z = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing="ij")
 570        else:
 571            z = np.array(axis_3_coords)
 572            x, y = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing="ij")
 573
 574        dose_grid = self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(x, y, z)
 575        profile = np.mean(dose_grid, axis=(1, 2))
 576        return profile
 577
 578        # pdd_dict["x_axis"] = z_values
 579        # pdd_dict["y_axis"] = np.array(dose_values)
 580        # return pdd_dict
 581
 582    def get_average_uncertainty(self, mask: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> float:
 583        r"""
 584        Purpose:
 585            - To calculate the average uncertainty normalized by dose
 586            in an optinal mask. The unit of uncertainty is in percentage.
 587        Inputs:
 588            - self:BrachyDose
 589            - mask: Optional[np.ndarray] := a mask to apply to the dose grid in [z, y, x] format.
 590        Outputs:
 591            - average_uncert:float := the average uncertainty in the dose grid in percentage.
 592        """
 593        # max_dose = self.dose_image.imageArray.max()
 594        # dose_mask = self.dose_image.imageArray < 0.2 * max_dose
 595        masked_uncert = ma.array(self.get_uncertainty_array(), mask=mask)
 596        average_uncert = ma.average(masked_uncert) * 100
 597        return average_uncert
 598
 599    def pad_3ddose(self, new_dims: list, new_origin: list) -> "BrachyDose":
 600        r"""a function to padd the grid and uncertainty in BrachyDose object and bring it to the desired dimensios.
 601        it will update all the aspects of the dose object to match the new dimensiosn.
 602        The voxels must have the same size! remember, python does z, y, x.
 603        inputs:
 604            self:BrachyDose
 605
 606            new_dims := a 1 by 3 list containing the new x, y and z dimensions:
 607                [new_z_dim, new_y_dim, new_x_dim]
 608
 609            new_origin := coordinates of the new origin_coordinates
 610                [x, y, z]
 611        """
 612        warnings.warn("This function is not tested yet", stacklevel=2)
 613        raise NotImplementedError(
 614            "This function is not needed. use resample from opentps instead!"
 615        )
 616        assert any(
 617            new_dims > self.dose_image.gridSize
 618        ), "since you are padding, the new dimensions should be larger than the input dimensions"
 619
 620        # calculate distances between the new and old origin_coordinates voxels.
 621        # if for an axis, the distance of origin_coordinatess is larger than the voxel size, use the new origin_coordinates
 622        # else, use the old top left
 623        origin_coordinates_distance = np.abs(new_origin - self.dose_image.origin)
 624        final_origin_coordinates = np.zeros(3)
 625        for i, distance in zip(range(3), origin_coordinates_distance):
 626            final_origin_coordinates[i] = (
 627                new_origin[i]
 628                if distance > self.dose_image.spacing[i]
 629                else self.dose_image.origin[i]
 630            )
 631
 632        # figure out how much padding to do before and after each axis
 633        padding = np.zeros([3, 2])
 634        for i in range(3):
 635            if final_origin_coordinates[i] == self.dose_image.origin[i]:
 636                # all padding goes to the end for this dose axis
 637                pad_before = 0
 638                pad_after = new_dims[i] - self.dose_image.gridSize[i]
 639            else:
 640                # all padding goes to the begining of the dose axis
 641                pad_before = new_dims[i] - self.dose_image.gridSize[i]
 642                pad_after = 0
 643            padding[i] = [pad_before, pad_after]
 644
 645        # pad the old dose grid to get the new grid!
 646        new_dose_grid = np.pad(
 647            self.dose_image.imageArray, tuple(padding.astype(int)), mode="edge"
 648        )
 649        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
 650            new_uncert = np.pad(
 651                self.uncertainty_image.imageArray,
 652                tuple(padding.astype(int)),
 653                mode="edge",
 654            )
 655        # fillout the new padded dose dictionary
 656        padded_dose = BrachyDose()
 657        padded_dose.dose_image = DoseImage(
 658            imageArray=new_dose_grid,
 659            origin=final_origin_coordinates,
 660            spacing=self.dose_image.spacing,
 661        )
 662        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
 663            padded_dose.uncertainty_image = DoseImage(
 664                imageArray=new_uncert,
 665                origin=final_origin_coordinates,
 666                spacing=self.dose_image.spacing,
 667            )
 668        self.get_voxel_edges()
 669        self.create_interpolation_function()
 670        return padded_dose
 671
 672    def write_to_3ddose(self, file_name: str):
 673        r"""
 674        Purpose:
 675            This function will write the contents of a BrachyDose onto a text file with .3ddose extension.
 676
 677        inputs:
 678            - self := a BrachyDose object containing the following keys:
 679                grid [x, y, z]
 680                uncert [x, y, z]
 681                voxel_size [x, y, z]
 682                origin_coordinates [x, y, z]
 683                axis [x, y, z]
 684
 685            - file_name := the directory path where the file will be written
 686        """
 687        file_name = os.path.abspath(file_name)
 688
 689        # dimensions = " ".join(map(str, np.flip(self.dose_image.gridSize.astype(int)))) + "\n"
 690        dimensions = " ".join(map(str, self.dose_image.gridSize.astype(int))) + "\n"
 691        x_axis = " ".join(map(str, (self.voxel_edges[0]) / 10)) + "\n"
 692        y_axis = " ".join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[1] / 10)) + "\n"
 693        z_axis = " ".join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[2] / 10)) + "\n"
 694        arr_flat = self.get_dose_array().flatten("C")
 695        formatted_str_array = np.char.mod(f"%.6f", arr_flat)
 696        dose_flattened = " ".join(formatted_str_array) + "\n"
 697        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
 698            arr_flat = self.get_uncertainty_array().flatten("C")
 699            formatted_str_array = np.char.mod(f"%.6f", arr_flat)
 700            uncertainty_flattened = (
 701                " ".join(formatted_str_array) + "\n"
 702            )
 703        else:
 704            uncertainty_flattened = " ".join(np.ones_like(formatted_str_array)) + "\n"
 705
 706        with open(file_name, "w") as file:
 707            lines = [
 708                dimensions,
 709                x_axis,
 710                y_axis,
 711                z_axis,
 712                dose_flattened,
 713                uncertainty_flattened,
 714            ]
 715            file.writelines(lines)
 716
 717    def write_to_nrrd(
 718        self,
 719        pth_output: Path,
 720        metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
 721        anatomical_coordinate_system: Literal[
 722            "LPS", "RAS"
 723        ] = "LPS",
 724    ):
 725        r"""
 726        Purpose:
 727            To save the contents of BrachyDose into a nrrd file.
 728        inputs:
 729            - pth_output := path where the dose nrrd file will be written to.
 730            - metadata := a dictionary containing the following meta data key values (should be changed later):
 731                "cancer site":
 732                "care center":
 733                "number of dwell positions":
 734                "number of segmented structures":
 735                "patient number":
 736                "Image content": "[3D dose, 3D uncertainty]"
 737            - anatomical_coordinate_system := the coordinate system of the dose grid. should be one of the following:
 738                "left-posterior-superior"
 739                "right-anterior-superior"
 740        outputs: Void
 741            writes [3D dose, 3D uncertainty], voxel size, origin (origin_coordinates), and metadata to the file_name_dose.nrrd
 742        """
 743        # check if the directory exists, if not create it. make sure the file extension is write.
 744        Path.mkdir(pth_output.parent, exist_ok=True)
 745        assert (
 746            str(pth_output).endswith(".nrrd")
 747        ), "the file should have '.nrrd' extension"
 748
 749        dose_array = self.get_dose_array()
 750        if self.uncertainty_image is None:
 751            uncertainty_array = np.ones_like(dose_array, dtype=np.float32)
 752        else:
 753            uncertainty_array = self.get_uncertainty_array()
 754        spacing = self.dose_image.spacing
 755        origin = self.dose_image.origin.tolist()
 756        dose_uncertainty_array, header = create_nrrd_object(
 757            dose_array=dose_array,
 758            uncertainty_array=uncertainty_array,
 759            spacing=spacing,
 760            origin=origin,
 761            anatomical_coordinate_system=anatomical_coordinate_system,
 762            metadata=metadata,
 763        )
 764        nrrd.write(str(pth_output), dose_uncertainty_array, header, index_order="C", compression_level=1)
 765

 809    def get_voxel_edges(self):
 810        r"""
 811        Purpose:
 812        - will calculate the axes coordinates for a 3ddose dictionary.
 813        Input:
 814            - self:BrachyDose
 815        Output:
 816            - axes:numpy.array() :=
 817            [[x_min:voxel_size:x_max],
 818            [y_min:voxel_size:y_max],
 819            [z_min:voxel_size:z_max]]
 820        """
 821        assert (
 822            self.dose_image is not None
 823        ), "dose image is not defined. please load a dose image first"
 824        voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
 825        self.voxel_edges = np.empty(len(voxel_centers), dtype=object)
 826        for i in range(len(voxel_centers)):
 827            self.voxel_edges[i] = voxel_centers[i] - self.dose_image.spacing[i] / 2.0
 828        return self.voxel_edges
 829
 830    def get_voxel_centers(self):
 831        r"""
 832        Purpose:
 833            - To calculate the voxel centers of the dose grid.
 834        Inputs:
 835            - self:BrachyDose
 836        Outputs:
 837            - voxel_centers := a numpy array containing the coordinates of the voxel centers for each axis.
 838        Dependencies:
 839            - Image3D.getMeshGridPositions()
 840        """
 841        assert (
 842            self.dose_image is not None
 843        ), "dose image is not defined. please load a dose image first"
 844        voxel_centers = np.empty(len(self.dose_image.origin), dtype=object)
 845        for i in range(len(self.dose_image.origin)):
 846            voxel_centers[i] = (
 847                self.dose_image.origin[i]
 848                + np.arange(self.dose_image.gridSize[i]) * self.dose_image.spacing[i]
 849            )
 850        return voxel_centers
 851
 852    def get_dose_at_coordinates(self, coords: Union[np.ndarray, List[float]], uncertainty = False) -> float:
 853        r"""
 854        Purpose:
 855            - Given a set of coordinates, this function will return the dose at that point.
 856        Inputs:
 857            - coords := a list of 3 coordinates [x, y, z] or a numpy array of shape (3,)
 858        Outputs:
 859            - dose := the dose at the given coordinates in Gy
 860        """
 861        assert len(coords) == 3, "coords should be a list of 3 coordinates"
 862        if uncertainty:
 863            assert self.uncertainty_image is not None, "uncertainty image is not defined"
 864            return self.uncertainty_image.getDataAtPosition(coords)
 865        else:
 866            return self.dose_image.getDataAtPosition(coords)
 867
 868    def get_uncertainty_at_coordinates(
 869        self, coords: Union[np.ndarray, List[float]]
 870    ) -> float:
 871        r"""
 872        Purpose:
 873            - Given a set of coordinates, this function will return the dose at that point.
 874        Inputs:
 875            - coords := a list of 3 coordinates [x, y, z] or a numpy array of shape (3,)
 876        Outputs:
 877            - dose := the dose at the given coordinates in Gy
 878        """
 879        assert len(coords) == 3, "coords should be a list of 3 coordinates"
 880        assert self.uncertainty_image is not None, "uncertainty image is not defined"

 883    def is_equal(self, new_brachy_dose) -> bool:
 884        r"""
 885        Purpose:
 886            - To compare if self:BrachyDose has the same attributes as an input BrachyDose
 887        Inputs:
 888            - new_brachy_dose: another BrachyDose object whose attributes may or may not contain
 889            equal info as the attributes of self.
 890        Outputs:
 891            True if attributes of new_brachy_dose are the same as self
 892            False otherwise
 893        """
 894        if not isinstance(new_brachy_dose, BrachyDose):
 895            warnings.warn("input must be of type BrachyDose", stacklevel=2)
 896            return False
 897        elif not np.all(
 898            np.isclose(
 899                self.dose_image.imageArray,
 900                new_brachy_dose.dose_image.imageArray,
 901                atol=1e-6,
 902            )
 903        ):
 904            warnings.warn("dose values are not the same", stacklevel=2)
 905            return False
 906        elif not np.all(
 907            np.isclose(
 908                np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges),
 909                np.concatenate(new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges),
 910                atol=1e-3,
 911            )
 912        ):
 913            warnings.warn("axis is not the same", stacklevel=2)
 914            return False
 915        elif not self.uncertainty_image is not None:
 916            if np.all(
 917                np.isclose(
 918                    self.uncertainty_image.imageArray,
 919                    new_brachy_dose.uncertainty_image.imageArray,
 920                    atol=1e-6,
 921                )
 922            ):
 923                warnings.warn("uncertainty is not the same", stacklevel=2)
 924                return False
 925        elif not np.array_equal(
 926            self.dose_image.gridSize, new_brachy_dose.dose_image.gridSize
 927        ):
 928            warnings.warn("num_voxels is not the same", stacklevel=2)
 929            return False
 930        elif not np.all(
 931            np.isclose(
 932                self.dose_image.spacing, new_brachy_dose.dose_image.spacing, atol=1e-3
 933            )
 934        ):
 935            warnings.warn("voxel_size is not the same", stacklevel=2)
 936            return False
 937        elif not np.all(
 938            np.isclose(
 939                self.dose_image.origin, new_brachy_dose.dose_image.origin, atol=1e-3
 940            )
 941        ):
 942            warnings.warn("origin_coordinates is not the same", stacklevel=2)
 943            return False
 944        else:
 945            return True
 946
 947    def crop_by_coordinates(
 948        self, coordinate_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True
 949    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
 950        r"""
 951        Purpose:
 952            - given a range of coordinate (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
 953            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly.
 954        Inputs:
 955            - self: BrachyDose object
 956            - coordinate_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on z, y and x axis
 957                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max],]
 958        Output:
 959            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range.
 960                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
 961        Dependencies:
 962            opentps.core.processing.imageProcessing.resampler3D.crop3DDataAroundBox
 963        """
 964        from opentps.core.processing.imageProcessing.resampler3D import (
 965            crop3DDataAroundBox,
 966        )
 967
 968        self.is_not_empty()
 969        assert coordinate_range.shape == (
 970            3,
 971            2,
 972        ), "coordinate_range should be a 3x2 array in x, y, z order"
 973        if inplace:
 974            crop3DDataAroundBox(self.dose_image, coordinate_range)
 975            if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
 976                crop3DDataAroundBox(self.uncertainty_image, coordinate_range)
 977            self.get_voxel_edges()
 978            self.create_interpolation_function()
 979            self.get_voxel_edges()
 980        else:
 981            new_dose: BrachyDose = copy.deepcopy(self)
 982            new_dose.crop_by_coordinates(coordinate_range, inplace=True)
 983            return new_dose
 984
 985    def crop_by_fraction(
 986        self, crop_fraction: List[float], inplace: Optional[bool] = True
 987    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
 988        r"""
 989        Purpose:
 990            - given the crop_fraction, this function will crop out 0.5*(1 - crop_fraction)*gridSizeInWorldUnit
 991            from the edges of the x and y, and z axis of dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of
 992            the attributes accordingly.
 993        Inputs:
 994            - self: BrachyDose object
 995            - crop_fraction := 3 floating point between 0 and 1 (one per axis for x, y, z axis), which is the fraction of the image axis
 996            that remains in the crop. for example, a crop ratio of [1, 0.5, 0.5] will keep the center of the x and y axis,
 997            plus minus 0.25*dimension of the image. The z axis will not be cropped.
 998                    +++++++++       ---------
 999                    +++++++++       --+++++--
1000                    +++++++++  ===> --+++++--
1001                    +++++++++       --+++++--
1002                    +++++++++       ---------
1003        Output:
1004            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range.
1005                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
1006        Dependencies:
1007            -self.crop_by_coordinates()
1008        """
1009        crop_fraction = np.array(crop_fraction)
1010        assert np.all(crop_fraction >= 0) and np.all(
1011            crop_fraction <= 1
1012        ), "the fraction should be between 0 and 1"
1013
1014        off_set = 0.5 * (1 - crop_fraction) * self.dose_image.gridSizeInWorldUnit
1015        new_origin_coords = self.dose_image.origin + off_set
1016        assert np.all(
1017            new_origin_coords >= self.dose_image.origin
1018        ), "new origin cannot be smaller than the original origin."
1019
1020        new_ending_coords = (
1021            self.dose_image.origin + self.dose_image.gridSizeInWorldUnit - off_set
1022        )
1023
1024        new_coords_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_coords, new_ending_coords])
1025
1026        return self.crop_by_coordinates(new_coords_range, inplace)
1027
1028    def crop_by_index(
1029        self, index_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True
1030    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
1031        r"""
1032        Purpose:
1033            - given a range of indicies (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
1034            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly.
1035        Inputs:
1036            - self: BrachyDose object
1037            - index_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on z, y and x axis
1038                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]]
1039        Output:
1040            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the index range.
1041        Dependencies:
1042            - self.crop_by_coordinates()
1043        """
1044
1045        # convert indicies to coordinates
1046        new_origin_coords = self.dose_image.getPositionFromVoxelIndex(index_range[:, 0])
1047        new_ending_coords = self.dose_image.getPositionFromVoxelIndex(index_range[:, 1])
1048        new_coords_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_coords, new_ending_coords])
1049        return self.crop_by_coordinates(new_coords_range, inplace)
1050
1051    def is_not_empty(self) -> bool:
1052        assert self.dose_image is not None, "error dose image is None"
1053        assert self.voxel_edges is not None, "error axis is None"
1054        return True

1069    def crop_by_contour(
1070        self,
1071        phantom_obj: BrachyPhantom,
1072        contour_name: str,
1073        inplace: Optional[bool] = True,
1074    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
1075        r"""
1076        Purpose:
1077            - based on the given phantom object, crop the BrachyDose object such
1078            that it only contains the smallest bounding box around the contour.
1079        Inputs:
1080            - self: BrachyDose object
1081            - phantom_obj: BrachyPhantom object
1082            - contour_name: str := the name of the contour to crop the dose around
1083            - inplace: bool := if True, the function will crop the dose in place, otherwise it will return a new dose object
1084        Outputs:
1085            - None or BrachyDose := if inplace is True, the function will return None, otherwise it will return a new BrachyDose object
1086        """
1087        from opentps.core.data import ROIMask
1088        from opentps.core.processing.imageProcessing.resampler3D import (
1089            resampleImage3DOnImage3D,
1090        )
1091        from opentps.core.processing.segmentation.segmentation3D import getBoxAroundROI
1092
1093        mask_dict = phantom_obj.get_structure_mask([contour_name], mask_type=ROIMask)
1094        resampled_mask = resampleImage3DOnImage3D(
1095            mask_dict[contour_name], self.density_image
1096        )
1097        box_around_mask = np.array(getBoxAroundROI(resampled_mask))
1098        return self.crop_by_coordinates(box_around_mask, inplace)
1099
1100    def multiply_dose_by_constant(
1101        self, scale_factor: float, scale_uncert: Optional[bool] = False
1102    ) -> None:
1103        r"""

1111        self.is_not_empty()
1112        self.dose_image.imageArray *= scale_factor
1113        if scale_uncert and self.uncertainty_image is not None:
1114            self.uncertainty_image.imageArray *= scale_factor

1166    def dose_with_empty_grid_like(dose_obj: "BrachyDose") -> "BrachyDose":
1167        r"""
1168        Purpose:
1169            - To create a new dose object with the same attributes as the input dose object,
1170            but with an empty grid and uncertainty.

1219    def dose_nans_to_number(self, number: float = -1, inplace: Optional[bool] = True
1220    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
1221        r"""
1222        Purpose:
1223            - Sometimes NaNs may be found in the dose grid of a brachydose
1224            object, for example in DoseComparison, where NaNs signify a masked region
1225            for plotting. However, we may not want to have them in our grid for analysis. 
1226            This function replaces NaNs with a specified number.
1227
1228        Inputs:
1229            - number: the number that will replace NaNs in the dose grid. Default is -1.
1230            - inplace: if True, the function will modify the current BrachyDose object, otherwise it will return a new BrachyDose object with the NaNs replaced.
1231        
1232        Outputs:
1233            - New BrachyDose object if inplace is False
1234        """
1235        if inplace:
1236            self.dose_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(self.dose_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1237            if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
1238                self.uncertainty_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(self.uncertainty_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1239            return None
1240        else:
1241            new_dose = copy.deepcopy(self)
1242            new_dose.dose_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(new_dose.dose_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1243            if new_dose.uncertainty_image is not None:
1244                new_dose.uncertainty_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(new_dose.uncertainty_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1245            return new_dose

Purpse: - This class holds information regarding a dose and uncertainty distribution as well as the fundamental functions that are applied on the dose. All doses are expressed in Gy and all the unit length is mm.

Attributes: - dose_image:DoseImage := DoseImage object holding the dose grid ([x, y, z]), as well as spacing, origin, and rotation ([x, y, z]) information. - uncertainty_image:DoseImage := DoseImage object holding the dose uncertainity grid ([x, y, z]), as well as spacing, origin, and rotation ([x, y, z]) information. - voxel_edges:np.ndarray := coorindates of voxel edges along x, y and z axis. - interpolation_function := RegularGridInterpolator object that allows for sampling of dose at arbitrary points ([x, y, z]). Functions: - load_file_to_brachydose - write_brachydose_to_file - load_from_3ddose - load_from_nrrd - load_from_npz - load_from_dicom - load_from_minidos - create_interpolation_function - extract_dose_values_from_coordinates - extract_profile_2d - extract_profile_1d - get_average_uncert - get_average_uncert_benchmark - pad_3ddose - write_to_3ddose - write_to_nrrd - write_to_npz - write_to_minidos - crop_by_coordinates - crop_by_index - crop_by_fraction

def load_file_to_brachydose( self, pth_dose_file: pathlib._local.Path, load_uncertainty: Optional[bool] = True) -> None: 
 97    def load_file_to_brachydose(
 98        self, pth_dose_file: Path, load_uncertainty: Optional[bool] = True,
 99    ) -> None:
100        r"""
101        Purpose:
102            - given the path to a file holding dose information, it will return
103        a BrachyDose object with the populated available attributes.
104
105        Inputs:
106            - pth_dose_file := path directory where the file containing the dose is. The file
107                extension could be ".3ddose", ".nrrd", ".dcm", or ".minidos"
108            - load_uncertainty := a boolean flag to load the uncertainty image if it is available.
109        Output:
110            - None := the contents of the file are loaded into the BrachyDose object.
111        Dependencies:
112            - load_from_3ddose()
113            - load_from_nrrd()
114            - load_from_dicom()
115            - create_interpolation_function()
116        """
117        if isinstance(pth_dose_file, tuple):
118            assert len(pth_dose_file) == 2, "If a tuple is provided, it must be of length 2"
119            assert isinstance(pth_dose_file[0], np.ndarray), "First element of the tuple must be a numpy array"
120            assert isinstance(pth_dose_file[1], defaultdict), "Second element of the tuple must be a dictionary"
121            self.load_from_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
122        else:
123            pth_dose_file = os.path.abspath(pth_dose_file)
124
125            file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
126
127            if file_extension == ".3ddose":
128                self.load_from_3ddose(pth_dose_file, load_uncertainty)
129            elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
130                self.load_from_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
131            elif file_extension == ".dcm":
132                self.load_from_dicom(pth_dose_file)
133            elif file_extension == ".gz" or file_extension == ".nii":
134                self.load_from_nifti(pth_dose_file)
135            elif file_extension == ".minidos":
136                raise NotImplementedError(
137                    "loading dose from .minidos file is not currently supported"
138                )
139            elif file_extension == ".bindose":
140                raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
141            else:
142                raise ValueError("file extension not recognized")
143            if self.dose_image is None:
144                raise ValueError("dose image not loaded")
145        if self.interpolation_function is None and self.dose_image is not None:
146            self.create_interpolation_function()

def write_brachydose_to_file(self, pth_dose_file: pathlib._local.Path | str) -> None: 
148    def write_brachydose_to_file(self, pth_dose_file: Path | str) -> None:
149        r"""
150        Purpose:
151            - To write a brachy dose object to the given file path. this function will automatically
152        detect the type of the output file and will call the right brachyDose writer function.
153        Inputs:
154            - pth_dose_file := path where the BrachyDose contents will be written to. The options
155            for output type are "3ddose", "nrrd", "npz", "minidos", "xz", and "zstd".
156        Dependencies:
157            - write_to_3ddose()
158            - write_to_nrrd()
159            - write_to_npz()
160            - write_to_minidos()
161            - write_to_xz()
162            - write_to_zstd()
163        Output:
164            - None := contents of self is written to "pth_dose_file"
165        """
166        pth_dose_file = Path(pth_dose_file)
167        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
168        pth_dose_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
169        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
170            self.write_to_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
171
172        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
173            self.write_to_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
174
175        elif file_extension == ".dcm":
176            self.write_to_dicom(pth_dose_file)
177
178        elif file_extension == ".npz":
179            self.write_to_npz(pth_dose_file)
180
181        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
182            self.write_to_minidos(pth_dose_file)
183
184        elif file_extension == ".xz":
185            self.write_to_xz(pth_dose_file)
186
187        elif file_extension == ".zstd":
188            self.write_to_zstd(pth_dose_file)
189
190        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
191            raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
192        else:
193            raise ValueError(
194                f"The input file name {pth_dose_file} is not supported. the supported \
195            file types are '.3ddose', '.nrrd', '.npz', '.minidos', '.xz', and '.zstd'"
196            )

Purpose: - To write a brachy dose object to the given file path. this function will automatically detect the type of the output file and will call the right brachyDose writer function. Inputs: - pth_dose_file := path where the BrachyDose contents will be written to. The options for output type are "3ddose", "nrrd", "npz", "minidos", "xz", and "zstd". Dependencies: - write_to_3ddose() - write_to_nrrd() - write_to_npz() - write_to_minidos() - write_to_xz() - write_to_zstd() Output: - None := contents of self is written to "pth_dose_file"

def load_from_3ddose( self, filename: pathlib._local.Path, load_uncertainty: Optional[bool] = True) -> None: 
198    def load_from_3ddose(
199        self, filename: Path, load_uncertainty: Optional[bool] = True
200    ) -> None:
201        r"""
202        Purpose:
203            - Given the path to a 3ddose file, load its content into self:BrachyDose.
204        Input:
205            - filename := path to a ".3ddose" file
206        Outputs:
207            - void := contents of self is updated.
208        Dependencies:
209            - numpy
210            - os
211        """
212        assert (
213            os.path.splitext(filename)[-1] == ".3ddose"
214        ), "this file should have '3ddose' extension."
215        path = filename
216        # print("Opening 3ddose at %s" % path)
217        with open(path, "rb") as newfile:
218            bench_voxels = [int(i) for i in newfile.readline().split()]
219            bench_x_pos = (
220                np.round(
221                    np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6
222                )
223                * 10
224            )
225            bench_y_pos = (
226                np.round(
227                    np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6
228                )
229                * 10
230            )
231            bench_z_pos = (
232                np.round(
233                    np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6
234                )
235                * 10
236            )
237
238            bench_spacing = np.array(
239                [
240                    bench_x_pos[1] - bench_x_pos[0],
241                    bench_y_pos[1] - bench_y_pos[0],
242                    bench_z_pos[1] - bench_z_pos[0],
243                ]
244            )
245            bench_origin = np.array(
246                [
247                    bench_x_pos[0] + bench_spacing[0] / 2,
248                    bench_y_pos[0] + bench_spacing[1] / 2,
249                    bench_z_pos[0] + bench_spacing[2] / 2,
250                ],
251                dtype=np.float32,
252            )
253
254            huge_dose_array = np.array(
255                newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32
256            )
257            try:
258                bench_dose = reshape(
259                    huge_dose_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0])
260                )
261            except ValueError as e:
262                print(f"Error in dose file {filename}: {e}", "\n")
263                bench_dose = None
264
265            if load_uncertainty:
266                try:
267                    huge_uncert_array = np.array(
268                        newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32
269                    )
270                    bench_uncert = reshape(
271                        huge_uncert_array,
272                        (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]),
273                    )
274                    self.uncertainty_image = DoseImage(
275                        # convert numpy zyx to xyz in opentps.
276                        imageArray=np.swapaxes(bench_uncert, 0, 2),
277                        origin=bench_origin,
278                        spacing=bench_spacing,
279                    )
280                except ValueError:
281                    print("Warning: No uncertainty in the 3ddose file", filename, "\n")
282
283            self.dose_image = DoseImage(
284                # convert numpy zyx to xyz in opentps.
285                imageArray=np.swapaxes(bench_dose, 0, 2),
286                origin=bench_origin,
287                spacing=bench_spacing,
288            )
289            self.voxel_edges = self.get_voxel_edges()

Purpose: - Given the path to a 3ddose file, load its content into self:BrachyDose. Input: - filename := path to a ".3ddose" file Outputs: - void := contents of self is updated. Dependencies: - numpy - os

def load_from_nrrd( self, pth_nrrd: pathlib._local.Path | tuple[numpy.ndarray, collections.defaultdict]) -> None: 
291    def load_from_nrrd(self, pth_nrrd: Path|tuple[np.ndarray, defaultdict]) -> None:
292        r"""
293        Purpose:
294            - given the path to a .nrrd dose file, it will load its content into self:BrachyDose
295        Inputs:
296            - pth_nrrd := Path to a .nrrd file writtern. by default, we assume c index ordering is done.
297        Outputs:
298            - void := contents of self is updated.
299        Dependencies:
300            - nrrd
301            - get_voxel_edges()
302        """
303        # nrrd.reader._READ_CHUNKSIZE = 500 * 1024 * 1024  # 500MB
304        if isinstance(pth_nrrd, tuple):
305            dose_uncertainty, header = pth_nrrd
306        else:
307            dose_uncertainty, header = nrrd.read(pth_nrrd, index_order="C")
308
309        if dose_uncertainty.shape[0] == 2:
310            dose_array = dose_uncertainty[0]
311            uncertainty_array = dose_uncertainty[1]
312        elif dose_uncertainty.shape[-1] == 2:
313            dose_array = dose_uncertainty[:, :, :, 0]
314            uncertainty_array = dose_uncertainty[:, :, :, 1]
315            affine = header.get("space directions")[1:]
316        else:
317            # print("Uncertainty not found in the nrrd file")
318            dose_array = dose_uncertainty
319            uncertainty_array = None
320            affine = header.get("space directions")
321
322        voxel_size = affine.diagonal()
323        origin_coordinates = np.array(header.get("space origin")).astype(np.float32)
324        orientation = header.get("space").split("-")
325        orientation = "".join([char[0].upper() for char in orientation])
326        self.dose_image = DoseImage(
327            # imageArray=np.swapaxes(dose_array, 0, 2),
328            origin=origin_coordinates,
329            spacing=voxel_size,
330        )
331        self.set_dose_array(dose_array)
332        self.uncertainty_image = (
333            DoseImage(
334                # imageArray=np.swapaxes(uncertainty_array, 0, 2),
335                origin=origin_coordinates,
336                spacing=voxel_size,
337            )
338            if uncertainty_array is not None
339            else None
340        )
341        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
342            self.set_uncertainty_array(uncertainty_array)
343        self.dose_image.to_lps(current_orientation=orientation)
344        self.voxel_edges = self.get_voxel_edges()

400    def load_from_nifti(self, pth_nifti: Path):
401        pth_nifti = Path(pth_nifti)
402        import nibabel as nib
403        dose_nifti = nib.load(str(pth_nifti))
404        orientation = "".join(nib.aff2axcodes(dose_nifti.affine))
405        dose_data = np.ascontiguousarray(dose_nifti.get_fdata())
406        origin = dose_nifti.affine[:3, 3]
407        spacing = dose_nifti.header.get("pixdim")[1:4]
408        origin = np.array([
409            origin[0] * np.sign(dose_nifti.affine[0][0]),
410            origin[1] * np.sign(dose_nifti.affine[1][1]),
411            origin[2] * np.sign(dose_nifti.affine[2][2]),
412        ])
413        self.dose_image = DoseImage(
414            imageArray=dose_data,
415            origin=origin,
416            spacing=spacing,
417        )
418        self.dose_image.to_lps(current_orientation=orientation)

437    def create_interpolation_function(self) -> None:
438        r"""
439        Purpose:
440            - To create an interpolation function for the dose grid.
441            it allows for sampling of dose at any arbitrary set of points.
442        Inputs:
443            - self:BrachyDose := the object must have the grid attribute populated.
444        Outputs:
445            - void := the interpolation function is stored in the object.
446        Dependencies:
447            - scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator()

450        self.interpolation_function = RegularGridInterpolator(
451            (voxel_centers[0], voxel_centers[1], voxel_centers[2]),
452            self.dose_image.imageArray,
453            bounds_error=False,
454            fill_value=0,
455        )

def extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(self, x, y, z, uncertainty=False): 
457    def extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(self, x, y, z, uncertainty = False):
458        # r""" """
459        # raise DeprecationWarning(
460        #    "This function is no longer supported due to migration to open tps. please use self.get_dose_at_coordinates() instead."
461        # )
462        # self.is_not_empty()
463        # if self.interpolation_function is None:
464        #    raise ValueError("interpolation function is not defined")
465        shape = []
466        axis = []
467        for coord in [z, y, x]:
468            if isinstance(coord, float):
469                coord_size = 1
470                axis.append([coord])
471            elif isinstance(coord, np.ndarray):
472                coord_size = coord.size
473                axis.append(coord)
474            else:
475                raise TypeError("x, y, and z should be either floats or numpy arrays")
476            shape.append(coord_size)
477        coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x = np.meshgrid(
478            [z], [y], [x], indexing="ij"
479        )
480        if not uncertainty:
481        # trunk-ignore(ruff/E731)
482            dose_grid_lambda = lambda xs, ys, zs: self.dose_image.getDataAtPosition(
483                (xs, ys, zs)
484            )
485            dose_grid_function = np.vectorize(dose_grid_lambda)
486            dose_grid = dose_grid_function(coord_grid_x, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_z)
487            dose_grid.reshape(shape)
488            return dose_grid.squeeze()
489        else:
490            uncertainty_grid_lambda = lambda xs, ys, zs: self.uncertainty_image.getDataAtPosition(
491                (xs, ys, zs)
492            )
493            uncertainty_grid_function = np.vectorize(uncertainty_grid_lambda)
494            uncertainty_grid = uncertainty_grid_function(coord_grid_x, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_z)
495            uncertainty_grid.reshape(shape)
496            return uncertainty_grid.squeeze()
def extract_profile_2d( self, axis_1_coords: numpy.ndarray, axis_2_coords: numpy.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str): 
498    def extract_profile_2d(
499        self,
500        axis_1_coords: np.ndarray,
501        axis_2_coords: np.ndarray,
502        plane_coord: float,
503        plane: str,
504    ):
505        if (
506            not isinstance(axis_1_coords, np.ndarray)
507            or not isinstance(axis_2_coords, np.ndarray)
508            or not isinstance(plane_coord, float)
509        ):
510            raise TypeError(
511                "axis_1_coords and axis_2_coords should be numpy arrays and plane_coord should be a float"
512            )
513        if plane == "xy":
514            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(

516            )
517        elif plane == "xz":
518            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
519                axis_1_coords, plane_coord, axis_2_coords
520            )
521        elif plane == "yz":
522            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(

524            )
525        elif plane == "yx":
526            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
527                axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, plane_coord
528            )
529        elif plane == "zx":

531                axis_2_coords, plane_coord, axis_1_coords
532            )
533        elif plane == "zy":

536            )
537        else:
538            raise ValueError(
539                "plane should be one of the following: 'xy', 'xz', 'yz', 'yx', 'zx', 'zy'"

def extract_profile_1d( self, axis: str, axis_1_coords: numpy.ndarray, axis_2_coords: numpy.ndarray, axis_3_coords: List[float]) -> numpy.ndarray: 
542    def extract_profile_1d(
543        self,
544        axis: str,
545        axis_1_coords: np.ndarray,
546        axis_2_coords: np.ndarray,
547        axis_3_coords: List[float],
548    ) -> np.ndarray:
549        r"""
550        Extracts a 1D line profile from the dose grid along the specified axis, given the coordinates of the other two axes and a list of coordinates along the axis of extraction.
551
552        Parameters:
553            - axis (str): the axis along which to extract the line profile. Must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'.
554            - axis_1_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the first axis, as a 1D numpy array.
555            - axis_2_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the second axis, as a 1D numpy array.
556            - axis_3_coords (List[float]): the coordinates along the axis of extraction, as a list of floats.
557
558        Returns:
559            - profile (np.ndarray): the line profile extracted from the dose grid, as a 1D numpy array.
560        """
561        if axis not in ["x", "y", "z"]:
562            raise ValueError("axis must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'")
563
564        if axis == "x":
565            x = np.array(axis_3_coords)
566            y, z = np.meshgrid(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, indexing="ij")
567        elif axis == "y":
568            y = np.array(axis_3_coords)
569            x, z = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing="ij")
570        else:
571            z = np.array(axis_3_coords)
572            x, y = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing="ij")
573
574        dose_grid = self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(x, y, z)
575        profile = np.mean(dose_grid, axis=(1, 2))
576        return profile
577

579        # pdd_dict["y_axis"] = np.array(dose_values)
580        # return pdd_dict

Returns: - profile (np.ndarray): the line profile extracted from the dose grid, as a 1D numpy array.

def get_average_uncertainty(self, mask: Optional[numpy.ndarray] = None) -> float: 
582    def get_average_uncertainty(self, mask: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> float:
583        r"""
584        Purpose:
585            - To calculate the average uncertainty normalized by dose
586            in an optinal mask. The unit of uncertainty is in percentage.
587        Inputs:
588            - self:BrachyDose
589            - mask: Optional[np.ndarray] := a mask to apply to the dose grid in [z, y, x] format.
590        Outputs:
591            - average_uncert:float := the average uncertainty in the dose grid in percentage.
592        """
593        # max_dose = self.dose_image.imageArray.max()
594        # dose_mask = self.dose_image.imageArray < 0.2 * max_dose
595        masked_uncert = ma.array(self.get_uncertainty_array(), mask=mask)
596        average_uncert = ma.average(masked_uncert) * 100
597        return average_uncert

def pad_3ddose( self, new_dims: list, new_origin: list) -> BrachyDose: 
599    def pad_3ddose(self, new_dims: list, new_origin: list) -> "BrachyDose":
600        r"""a function to padd the grid and uncertainty in BrachyDose object and bring it to the desired dimensios.
601        it will update all the aspects of the dose object to match the new dimensiosn.
602        The voxels must have the same size! remember, python does z, y, x.
603        inputs:
604            self:BrachyDose
605
606            new_dims := a 1 by 3 list containing the new x, y and z dimensions:
607                [new_z_dim, new_y_dim, new_x_dim]
608
609            new_origin := coordinates of the new origin_coordinates
610                [x, y, z]
611        """
612        warnings.warn("This function is not tested yet", stacklevel=2)
613        raise NotImplementedError(
614            "This function is not needed. use resample from opentps instead!"
615        )
616        assert any(
617            new_dims > self.dose_image.gridSize
618        ), "since you are padding, the new dimensions should be larger than the input dimensions"
619
620        # calculate distances between the new and old origin_coordinates voxels.
621        # if for an axis, the distance of origin_coordinatess is larger than the voxel size, use the new origin_coordinates
622        # else, use the old top left
623        origin_coordinates_distance = np.abs(new_origin - self.dose_image.origin)
624        final_origin_coordinates = np.zeros(3)
625        for i, distance in zip(range(3), origin_coordinates_distance):
626            final_origin_coordinates[i] = (
627                new_origin[i]
628                if distance > self.dose_image.spacing[i]
629                else self.dose_image.origin[i]
630            )
631
632        # figure out how much padding to do before and after each axis
633        padding = np.zeros([3, 2])
634        for i in range(3):
635            if final_origin_coordinates[i] == self.dose_image.origin[i]:
636                # all padding goes to the end for this dose axis
637                pad_before = 0
638                pad_after = new_dims[i] - self.dose_image.gridSize[i]
639            else:
640                # all padding goes to the begining of the dose axis
641                pad_before = new_dims[i] - self.dose_image.gridSize[i]
642                pad_after = 0
643            padding[i] = [pad_before, pad_after]
644
645        # pad the old dose grid to get the new grid!
646        new_dose_grid = np.pad(
647            self.dose_image.imageArray, tuple(padding.astype(int)), mode="edge"
648        )
649        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
650            new_uncert = np.pad(
651                self.uncertainty_image.imageArray,
652                tuple(padding.astype(int)),
653                mode="edge",
654            )
655        # fillout the new padded dose dictionary
656        padded_dose = BrachyDose()
657        padded_dose.dose_image = DoseImage(
658            imageArray=new_dose_grid,
659            origin=final_origin_coordinates,
660            spacing=self.dose_image.spacing,
661        )
662        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
663            padded_dose.uncertainty_image = DoseImage(
664                imageArray=new_uncert,
665                origin=final_origin_coordinates,
666                spacing=self.dose_image.spacing,
667            )
668        self.get_voxel_edges()
669        self.create_interpolation_function()
670        return padded_dose

new_dims := a 1 by 3 list containing the new x, y and z dimensions:

def write_to_3ddose(self, file_name: str): 
672    def write_to_3ddose(self, file_name: str):
673        r"""
674        Purpose:
675            This function will write the contents of a BrachyDose onto a text file with .3ddose extension.
676
677        inputs:
678            - self := a BrachyDose object containing the following keys:
679                grid [x, y, z]
680                uncert [x, y, z]
681                voxel_size [x, y, z]
682                origin_coordinates [x, y, z]
683                axis [x, y, z]
684
685            - file_name := the directory path where the file will be written
686        """
687        file_name = os.path.abspath(file_name)
688
689        # dimensions = " ".join(map(str, np.flip(self.dose_image.gridSize.astype(int)))) + "\n"
690        dimensions = " ".join(map(str, self.dose_image.gridSize.astype(int))) + "\n"
691        x_axis = " ".join(map(str, (self.voxel_edges[0]) / 10)) + "\n"
692        y_axis = " ".join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[1] / 10)) + "\n"
693        z_axis = " ".join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[2] / 10)) + "\n"
694        arr_flat = self.get_dose_array().flatten("C")
695        formatted_str_array = np.char.mod(f"%.6f", arr_flat)
696        dose_flattened = " ".join(formatted_str_array) + "\n"
697        if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
698            arr_flat = self.get_uncertainty_array().flatten("C")
699            formatted_str_array = np.char.mod(f"%.6f", arr_flat)
700            uncertainty_flattened = (
701                " ".join(formatted_str_array) + "\n"
702            )
703        else:
704            uncertainty_flattened = " ".join(np.ones_like(formatted_str_array)) + "\n"
705
706        with open(file_name, "w") as file:
707            lines = [
708                dimensions,
709                x_axis,
710                y_axis,
711                z_axis,
712                dose_flattened,
713                uncertainty_flattened,
714            ]
715            file.writelines(lines)

def write_to_nrrd( self, pth_output: pathlib._local.Path, metadata: Optional[dict] = None, anatomical_coordinate_system: Literal['LPS', 'RAS'] = 'LPS'): 
717    def write_to_nrrd(
718        self,
719        pth_output: Path,
720        metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
721        anatomical_coordinate_system: Literal[
722            "LPS", "RAS"
723        ] = "LPS",
724    ):
725        r"""
726        Purpose:
727            To save the contents of BrachyDose into a nrrd file.
728        inputs:
729            - pth_output := path where the dose nrrd file will be written to.
730            - metadata := a dictionary containing the following meta data key values (should be changed later):
731                "cancer site":
732                "care center":
733                "number of dwell positions":
734                "number of segmented structures":
735                "patient number":
736                "Image content": "[3D dose, 3D uncertainty]"
737            - anatomical_coordinate_system := the coordinate system of the dose grid. should be one of the following:
738                "left-posterior-superior"
739                "right-anterior-superior"
740        outputs: Void
741            writes [3D dose, 3D uncertainty], voxel size, origin (origin_coordinates), and metadata to the file_name_dose.nrrd
742        """
743        # check if the directory exists, if not create it. make sure the file extension is write.
744        Path.mkdir(pth_output.parent, exist_ok=True)
745        assert (
746            str(pth_output).endswith(".nrrd")
747        ), "the file should have '.nrrd' extension"
748
749        dose_array = self.get_dose_array()
750        if self.uncertainty_image is None:
751            uncertainty_array = np.ones_like(dose_array, dtype=np.float32)
752        else:
753            uncertainty_array = self.get_uncertainty_array()
754        spacing = self.dose_image.spacing
755        origin = self.dose_image.origin.tolist()
756        dose_uncertainty_array, header = create_nrrd_object(
757            dose_array=dose_array,
758            uncertainty_array=uncertainty_array,
759            spacing=spacing,
760            origin=origin,
761            anatomical_coordinate_system=anatomical_coordinate_system,
762            metadata=metadata,
763        )
764        nrrd.write(str(pth_output), dose_uncertainty_array, header, index_order="C", compression_level=1)

Purpose: To save the contents of BrachyDose into a nrrd file. inputs: - pth_output := path where the dose nrrd file will be written to. - metadata := a dictionary containing the following meta data key values (should be changed later): "cancer site": "care center": "number of dwell positions": "number of segmented structures": "patient number": "Image content": "[3D dose, 3D uncertainty]" - anatomical_coordinate_system := the coordinate system of the dose grid. should be one of the following: "left-posterior-superior" "right-anterior-superior" outputs: Void writes [3D dose, 3D uncertainty], voxel size, origin (origin_coordinates), and metadata to the file_name_dose.nrrd

def write_to_npz(self, file_name: str): 
766    def write_to_npz(self, file_name: str):
767        r"""
768        Purpose:
769            To save the contents of BrachyDose into a npz file, which is numpy compressed.
770        inputs:
771            - self := BrachyDose object
772            - file_name := path where the dose npz file will be written to.
773        outputs: Void
774            writes the contents of self:BrachyDose to the file_name.
775        """
776
777        assert (
778            os.path.splitext(file_name)[-1] == ".npz"
779        ), "the file name should have '.npz' extension."
780
781        np.savez_compressed(

def get_voxel_edges(self): 
809    def get_voxel_edges(self):
810        r"""
811        Purpose:
812        - will calculate the axes coordinates for a 3ddose dictionary.
813        Input:
814            - self:BrachyDose
815        Output:
816            - axes:numpy.array() :=
817            [[x_min:voxel_size:x_max],
818            [y_min:voxel_size:y_max],
819            [z_min:voxel_size:z_max]]
820        """
821        assert (
822            self.dose_image is not None
823        ), "dose image is not defined. please load a dose image first"
824        voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
825        self.voxel_edges = np.empty(len(voxel_centers), dtype=object)
826        for i in range(len(voxel_centers)):
827            self.voxel_edges[i] = voxel_centers[i] - self.dose_image.spacing[i] / 2.0
828        return self.voxel_edges
