def get_voxel_centers(self): 
830    def get_voxel_centers(self):
831        r"""
832        Purpose:
833            - To calculate the voxel centers of the dose grid.
834        Inputs:
835            - self:BrachyDose
836        Outputs:
837            - voxel_centers := a numpy array containing the coordinates of the voxel centers for each axis.
838        Dependencies:
839            - Image3D.getMeshGridPositions()
840        """
841        assert (
842            self.dose_image is not None
843        ), "dose image is not defined. please load a dose image first"
844        voxel_centers = np.empty(len(self.dose_image.origin), dtype=object)
845        for i in range(len(self.dose_image.origin)):
846            voxel_centers[i] = (
847                self.dose_image.origin[i]
848                + np.arange(self.dose_image.gridSize[i]) * self.dose_image.spacing[i]
849            )
850        return voxel_centers

def is_equal(self, new_brachy_dose) -> bool: 
883    def is_equal(self, new_brachy_dose) -> bool:
884        r"""
885        Purpose:
886            - To compare if self:BrachyDose has the same attributes as an input BrachyDose
887        Inputs:
888            - new_brachy_dose: another BrachyDose object whose attributes may or may not contain
889            equal info as the attributes of self.
890        Outputs:
891            True if attributes of new_brachy_dose are the same as self
892            False otherwise
893        """
894        if not isinstance(new_brachy_dose, BrachyDose):
895            warnings.warn("input must be of type BrachyDose", stacklevel=2)
896            return False
897        elif not np.all(
898            np.isclose(
899                self.dose_image.imageArray,
900                new_brachy_dose.dose_image.imageArray,
901                atol=1e-6,
902            )
903        ):
904            warnings.warn("dose values are not the same", stacklevel=2)
905            return False
906        elif not np.all(
907            np.isclose(
908                np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges),
909                np.concatenate(new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges),
910                atol=1e-3,
911            )
912        ):
913            warnings.warn("axis is not the same", stacklevel=2)
914            return False
915        elif not self.uncertainty_image is not None:
916            if np.all(
917                np.isclose(
918                    self.uncertainty_image.imageArray,
919                    new_brachy_dose.uncertainty_image.imageArray,
920                    atol=1e-6,
921                )
922            ):
923                warnings.warn("uncertainty is not the same", stacklevel=2)
924                return False
925        elif not np.array_equal(
926            self.dose_image.gridSize, new_brachy_dose.dose_image.gridSize
927        ):
928            warnings.warn("num_voxels is not the same", stacklevel=2)
929            return False
930        elif not np.all(
931            np.isclose(
932                self.dose_image.spacing, new_brachy_dose.dose_image.spacing, atol=1e-3
933            )
934        ):
935            warnings.warn("voxel_size is not the same", stacklevel=2)
936            return False
937        elif not np.all(
938            np.isclose(
939                self.dose_image.origin, new_brachy_dose.dose_image.origin, atol=1e-3
940            )
941        ):
942            warnings.warn("origin_coordinates is not the same", stacklevel=2)
943            return False
944        else:
945            return True

Purpose: - To compare if self:BrachyDose has the same attributes as an input BrachyDose Inputs: - new_brachy_dose: another BrachyDose object whose attributes may or may not contain equal info as the attributes of self. Outputs: True if attributes of new_brachy_dose are the same as self False otherwise

def crop_by_coordinates( self, coordinate_range: <built-in function array>, inplace: Optional[bool] = True) -> Optional[BrachyDose]: 
947    def crop_by_coordinates(
948        self, coordinate_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True
949    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
950        r"""
951        Purpose:
952            - given a range of coordinate (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
953            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly.
954        Inputs:
955            - self: BrachyDose object
956            - coordinate_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on z, y and x axis
957                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max],]
958        Output:
959            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range.
960                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
961        Dependencies:
962            opentps.core.processing.imageProcessing.resampler3D.crop3DDataAroundBox
963        """
964        from opentps.core.processing.imageProcessing.resampler3D import (
965            crop3DDataAroundBox,
966        )
967
968        self.is_not_empty()
969        assert coordinate_range.shape == (
970            3,
971            2,
972        ), "coordinate_range should be a 3x2 array in x, y, z order"
973        if inplace:
974            crop3DDataAroundBox(self.dose_image, coordinate_range)
975            if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
976                crop3DDataAroundBox(self.uncertainty_image, coordinate_range)
977            self.get_voxel_edges()
978            self.create_interpolation_function()
979            self.get_voxel_edges()
980        else:
981            new_dose: BrachyDose = copy.deepcopy(self)
982            new_dose.crop_by_coordinates(coordinate_range, inplace=True)
983            return new_dose

Purpose: - given a range of coordinate (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. Inputs: - self: BrachyDose object - coordinate_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on z, y and x axis [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max],] Output: - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change Dependencies: opentps.core.processing.imageProcessing.resampler3D.crop3DDataAroundBox

def crop_by_fraction( self, crop_fraction: List[float], inplace: Optional[bool] = True) -> Optional[BrachyDose]: 
 985    def crop_by_fraction(
 986        self, crop_fraction: List[float], inplace: Optional[bool] = True
 987    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
 988        r"""
 989        Purpose:
 990            - given the crop_fraction, this function will crop out 0.5*(1 - crop_fraction)*gridSizeInWorldUnit
 991            from the edges of the x and y, and z axis of dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of
 992            the attributes accordingly.
 993        Inputs:
 994            - self: BrachyDose object
 995            - crop_fraction := 3 floating point between 0 and 1 (one per axis for x, y, z axis), which is the fraction of the image axis
 996            that remains in the crop. for example, a crop ratio of [1, 0.5, 0.5] will keep the center of the x and y axis,
 997            plus minus 0.25*dimension of the image. The z axis will not be cropped.
 998                    +++++++++       ---------
 999                    +++++++++       --+++++--
1000                    +++++++++  ===> --+++++--
1001                    +++++++++       --+++++--
1002                    +++++++++       ---------
1003        Output:
1004            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range.
1005                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
1006        Dependencies:
1007            -self.crop_by_coordinates()
1008        """
1009        crop_fraction = np.array(crop_fraction)
1010        assert np.all(crop_fraction >= 0) and np.all(
1011            crop_fraction <= 1
1012        ), "the fraction should be between 0 and 1"
1013
1014        off_set = 0.5 * (1 - crop_fraction) * self.dose_image.gridSizeInWorldUnit
1015        new_origin_coords = self.dose_image.origin + off_set
1016        assert np.all(
1017            new_origin_coords >= self.dose_image.origin
1018        ), "new origin cannot be smaller than the original origin."
1019
1020        new_ending_coords = (
1021            self.dose_image.origin + self.dose_image.gridSizeInWorldUnit - off_set
1022        )
1023
1024        new_coords_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_coords, new_ending_coords])
1025
1026        return self.crop_by_coordinates(new_coords_range, inplace)

Purpose: - given the crop_fraction, this function will crop out 0.5*(1 - crop_fraction)gridSizeInWorldUnit from the edges of the x and y, and z axis of dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. Inputs: - self: BrachyDose object - crop_fraction := 3 floating point between 0 and 1 (one per axis for x, y, z axis), which is the fraction of the image axis that remains in the crop. for example, a crop ratio of [1, 0.5, 0.5] will keep the center of the x and y axis, plus minus 0.25dimension of the image. The z axis will not be cropped. +++++++++ --------- +++++++++ --+++++-- +++++++++ ===> --+++++-- +++++++++ --+++++-- +++++++++ --------- Output: - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change Dependencies: -self.crop_by_coordinates()

def crop_by_contour( self, phantom_obj: brachyutils.geometry.BrachyPhantom, contour_name: str, inplace: Optional[bool] = True) -> Optional[BrachyDose]: 
1069    def crop_by_contour(
1070        self,
1071        phantom_obj: BrachyPhantom,
1072        contour_name: str,
1073        inplace: Optional[bool] = True,
1074    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
1075        r"""
1076        Purpose:
1077            - based on the given phantom object, crop the BrachyDose object such
1078            that it only contains the smallest bounding box around the contour.
1079        Inputs:
1080            - self: BrachyDose object
1081            - phantom_obj: BrachyPhantom object
1082            - contour_name: str := the name of the contour to crop the dose around
1083            - inplace: bool := if True, the function will crop the dose in place, otherwise it will return a new dose object
1084        Outputs:
1085            - None or BrachyDose := if inplace is True, the function will return None, otherwise it will return a new BrachyDose object
1086        """
1087        from opentps.core.data import ROIMask
1088        from opentps.core.processing.imageProcessing.resampler3D import (
1089            resampleImage3DOnImage3D,
1090        )
1091        from opentps.core.processing.segmentation.segmentation3D import getBoxAroundROI
1092
1093        mask_dict = phantom_obj.get_structure_mask([contour_name], mask_type=ROIMask)
1094        resampled_mask = resampleImage3DOnImage3D(
1095            mask_dict[contour_name], self.density_image
1096        )
1097        box_around_mask = np.array(getBoxAroundROI(resampled_mask))
1098        return self.crop_by_coordinates(box_around_mask, inplace)

Purpose: - based on the given phantom object, crop the BrachyDose object such that it only contains the smallest bounding box around the contour. Inputs: - self: BrachyDose object - phantom_obj: BrachyPhantom object - contour_name: str := the name of the contour to crop the dose around - inplace: bool := if True, the function will crop the dose in place, otherwise it will return a new dose object Outputs: - None or BrachyDose := if inplace is True, the function will return None, otherwise it will return a new BrachyDose object

def dose_with_ones_grid_like( dose_obj: BrachyDose) -> BrachyDose: 
1190    @staticmethod
1191    def dose_with_ones_grid_like(dose_obj: "BrachyDose") -> "BrachyDose":
1192        r"""
1193        Purpose:
1194            - To create a new dose object with the same attributes as the input dose object,
1195            but with a grid and uncertainty filled with ones.
1196
1197        Inputs:
1198            - doseObj: BrachyDose object
1199
1200        Outputs:

1202        """
1203        new_dose = BrachyDose()
1204        new_dose.dose_image = DoseImage(
1205            imageArray=np.ones_like(dose_obj.dose_image.imageArray),
1206            origin=dose_obj.dose_image.origin,
1207            spacing=dose_obj.dose_image.spacing,
1208        )
1209        if dose_obj.uncertainty_image is not None:
1210            new_dose.uncertainty_image = DoseImage(
1211                imageArray=np.ones_like(dose_obj.uncertainty_image.imageArray),
1212                origin=dose_obj.uncertainty_image.origin,
1213                spacing=dose_obj.uncertainty_image.spacing,
1214            )
1215        new_dose.get_voxel_edges()
1216        new_dose.create_interpolation_function()
1217        return new_dose

Purpose: - To create a new dose object with the same attributes as the input dose object, but with a grid and uncertainty filled with ones.

Inputs: - doseObj: BrachyDose object

Outputs: ones_dose: BrachyDose object with grid and uncertainty filled with ones

def dose_nans_to_number( self, number: float = -1, inplace: Optional[bool] = True) -> Optional[BrachyDose]: 
1219    def dose_nans_to_number(self, number: float = -1, inplace: Optional[bool] = True
1220    ) -> Union[None, "BrachyDose"]:
1221        r"""
1222        Purpose:
1223            - Sometimes NaNs may be found in the dose grid of a brachydose
1224            object, for example in DoseComparison, where NaNs signify a masked region
1225            for plotting. However, we may not want to have them in our grid for analysis. 
1226            This function replaces NaNs with a specified number.
1227
1228        Inputs:
1229            - number: the number that will replace NaNs in the dose grid. Default is -1.
1230            - inplace: if True, the function will modify the current BrachyDose object, otherwise it will return a new BrachyDose object with the NaNs replaced.
1231        
1232        Outputs:
1233            - New BrachyDose object if inplace is False
1234        """
1235        if inplace:
1236            self.dose_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(self.dose_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1237            if self.uncertainty_image is not None:
1238                self.uncertainty_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(self.uncertainty_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1239            return None
1240        else:
1241            new_dose = copy.deepcopy(self)
1242            new_dose.dose_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(new_dose.dose_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1243            if new_dose.uncertainty_image is not None:
1244                new_dose.uncertainty_image.imageArray = np.nan_to_num(new_dose.uncertainty_image.imageArray, nan=number)
1245            return new_dose

class BrachyDoseComparison: 
 21class BrachyDoseComparison:
 22    r"""
 23    ### Purpose:
 24    - A class to compare two BrachyDose objects by computing the percent difference and gamma index.
 25    
 26    ### Attributes:
 27    - gamma_kwargs (dict): Keyword arguments for the pymedphys gamma index function. Please
 28    see pymedphys.gamma for more details
 29    - dose1 (BrachyDose): The first BrachyDose object (reference).
 30    - dose2 (BrachyDose): The second BrachyDose object (test), to resampled on the grid of dose1 with extrapolated points set to 0.
 31    - voxel_centers (np.ndarray): The voxel centers of the dose grid.
 32    - dose_2_grid_resampled (np.ndarray): The dose grid of dose2 resampled to the grid of dose1.
 33    - percent_difference (BrachyDose): The percent difference between dose1 and dose2.
 34    - gamma_index (BrachyDose): The gamma index between dose1 and dose2.
 35    - gamma_dose_percent_threshold (float): The gamma dose percent threshold.
 36    - gamma_distance_threshold (float): The gamma distance threshold in mm.
 37    - gamma_kwargs (dict): The kwargs for the gamma index function.
 38    - prescription_dose (float): The prescription dose of the dose grid.
 39    - max_gamma (float): The maximum gamma index value.
 40    - gamma_pass_ratio (float): The ratio of gamma index values passing the threshold.
 41    
 42    ### Methods:
 43    - __init__(dose1, dose2, gamma_dose_percent_threshold, gamma_distance_threshold_mm, compute_percent_difference=True, compute_gamma_index=True, prescription_dose=None, max_gamma=None, path=None, gamma_kwargs=gamma_kwargs)
 44    - plot_2d_dose_comparison(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane, plot_titles)
 45    - compute_percent_difference()
 46    - compute_gamma_index()
 47    - save_comparison_object(path=None)
 48    - load_comparison_object(path=None)
 49
 50    """
 51
 52    default_gamma_kwargs : dict = {
 53        "lower_percent_dose_cutoff": 5,
 54        "interp_fraction": 10,
 55        "local_gamma": False,
 56        # "global_normalisation": None,
 57        "skip_once_passed": True,
 58        "max_gamma": 1.1
 59    }
 60
 61    def __init__(
 62        self,
 63        dose1: BrachyDose,
 64        dose2: BrachyDose,
 65        gamma_dose_percent_threshold: float = 3.0,
 66        gamma_distance_threshold_mm: float = 3.0,
 67        compute_percent_difference=True,
 68        prescription_dose: float = None,
 69        compute_dose_ratios: bool = False,
 70        compute_gamma_index=True,
 71        path=None,
 72        gamma_kwargs: dict = default_gamma_kwargs,
 73        positive_percent_difference: bool = True,
 74        percent_difference_range: tuple = (0, 200),
 75        dose_mask: BrachyDose = None
 76    ):
 77        r"""
 78        ### Purpose:
 79        - to compare two BrachyDose objects. The comparison is done by computing the percent difference and gamma index.
 80        The gamma index is computed using the pymedphys gamma function. The result of the comparison is stored in the object and
 81        can be viewed using the plot_2d_dose_comparison function.
 82
 83        ### Inputs:
 84        - dose1: BrachyDose object
 85        - dose2: BrachyDose object
 86        - gamma_dose_percent_threshold: float := the gamma dose percent threshold
 87        - gamma_distance_threshold_mm: float := the gamma distance threshold in mm
 88        - compute_percent_difference: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed
 89        - compute_gamma_index: bool := if True, the gamma index will be computed
 90        - prescription_dose: float := the prescription dose of the dose grid
 91        - max_gamma: float := the maximum gamma index value
 92        - path: str := the path to the comparison object
 93        - gamma_kwargs: dict := the kwargs for the gamma index function
 94        - positive_percent_difference: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed with or without absolute value
 95        - percent_difference_range: tuple := the range of the percent difference used in plotting
 96        - dose_mask: BrachyDose := a mask to apply to the dose comparison, excluding any voxels where the mask is valued <0
 97
 98        ### Outputs:
 99        Object containing the following attributes:
100        - dose1: BrachyDose object
101        - dose2: BrachyDose object, resampled on the grid of dose1 with extrapolated
102            points set to 0
103        - voxel_centers: numpy array := the voxel centers of the dose grid
104        - dose_2_grid_resampled: numpy array := the dose grid of dose2 resampled to the grid of dose1
105        - percent_difference: BrachyDose object := the percent difference between dose1 and dose2
106        - gamma_index: BrachyDose object := the gamma index between dose1 and dose2
107        - gamma_dose_percent_threshold: float := the gamma dose percent threshold
108        - gamma_distance_threshold: float := the gamma distance threshold in mm
109        - gamma_kwargs: dict := the kwargs for the gamma index function
110        - plot_max_dose_percent_of_prescription : int = default 300%, can be tuned to get a good dynamic range for plots
111        and The following functions:
112            - compute_percent_difference: void := to compute the percent difference between dose1 and dose2
113            - compute_gamma_index: void := to compute the gamma index between dose1 and dose2
114            - plot_2d_dose_comparison: void := to plot the 2d dose comparison
115            - save_comparison_object
116            - load_comparison_object
117        """
118        # note: we will not use DoseComparisonImageProvider from OpenTPS
119        # since the gamma index capabilities are not yet implemented
120        # provide no dose to just load a file
121        if dose1 is None and dose2 is None:
122            self.load_comparison_object(path)
123            return
124
125        self.dose1 = dose1
126        self.dose2 = dose2
127        # axis is taken from the first dose provided
128        self.voxel_centers = dose1.get_voxel_centers()
129        # print("Before resample", self.dose2.dose_image is None)
130        self.dose2.dose_image.resampleOn(dose1.dose_image, fillValue=0)
131        # print("After resample", self.dose2.dose_image is None)
132        self.percent_difference_local: BrachyDose = None
133        self.percent_difference_global: BrachyDose = None
134        self.dose_ratio: BrachyDose = None
135        # self.dose_comparision_image_provider = DoseComparisonImageProvider()
136        self.gamma_index: BrachyDose = None
137        self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold = gamma_dose_percent_threshold
138        self.gamma_kwargs = BrachyDoseComparison.default_gamma_kwargs
139        self.gamma_kwargs.update(gamma_kwargs) #in case the user wants to change the default
140        self.plot_max_dose_percent_of_prescription : int = 200
141        self.prescription_dose = (
142            gamma_kwargs.get("global_normalisation", 1.0) 
143            if prescription_dose is None 
144            else prescription_dose
145            )
146        self.gamma_kwargs["global_normalisation"] = self.prescription_dose
147        self.max_gamma = gamma_kwargs.get("max_gamma", 1.1)
148        self.percent_difference_range = percent_difference_range
149        self.dose_mask = dose_mask if dose_mask is not None else BrachyDose.dose_with_ones_grid_like(self.dose1)
150        # axes values are assumed in cm from the 3ddose formalism
151        # gamma distance thresholds are usually provided in mm
152        # pymedphys documentation indicates that the threshold unit must match the axis
153        # despite the name of the function input containing 'mm'
154        self.gamma_distance_threshold = gamma_distance_threshold_mm
155        if compute_percent_difference:
156            self.compute_percent_difference(positive_percent_difference, local = True)
157            self.compute_percent_difference(positive_percent_difference, local = False)
158        if compute_gamma_index:
159            self.compute_gamma_index()
160        if compute_dose_ratios:
161            self.compute_dose_ratios()

349    def compute_percent_difference(self, positive_percent_difference: bool = True, local: bool = True):
350        """
351        ### Purpose:
352        - Compute the local or global percent difference between two dose distributions.
353        self.dose1 is the reference and self.dose2 is the test dose.
354        See TG-372 for exact definitions
355        
356        ### Inputs:
357        - positive_percent_difference: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed with or without
358        absolute value
359        - local: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed locally; otherwise globally
360
361        ### Outputs:
362        - None. but updates the following attributes of the object:
363        - percent_difference_local: BrachyDose object := the local percent difference between dose1 and dose2
364        - percent_difference_global: BrachyDose object := the global percent difference between dose1 and dose2
365        """
366        #make sure there's no 0s in the ref dose to prevent division by 0
367        self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray == 0] = 1e-6 
368        if local:
369            self.percent_difference_local = BrachyDose.dose_with_empty_grid_like(self.dose1)
370            if positive_percent_difference:
371                self.percent_difference_local.dose_image.imageArray = (
372                    np.abs(self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray)
373                    / self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
374                    * 100.0
375                )
376            else:
377                self.percent_difference_local.dose_image.imageArray = (
378                    self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
379                ) * 100.0 / self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
380            if self.dose_mask is not None:
381                self.percent_difference_local.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose_mask.dose_image.imageArray < 0] = np.nan
382
383        else:
384            self.percent_difference_global = BrachyDose.dose_with_empty_grid_like(self.dose1)
385            if positive_percent_difference:
386                self.percent_difference_global.dose_image.imageArray = (
387                    np.abs(self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray)
388                    / self.prescription_dose
389                    * 100.0
390                )
391            else:
392                self.percent_difference_global.dose_image.imageArray = (
393                    self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
394                ) * 100.0 / self.prescription_dose
395
396            if self.dose_mask is not None:
397                self.percent_difference_global.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose_mask.dose_image.imageArray < 0] = np.nan
398
399    def compute_gamma_index(self):
400        """
401        ### Purpose:
402        - Compute the gamma index between two dose distributions.
403        This method calculates the gamma index, which is a quantitative measure
404        of the agreement between two dose distributions. The gamma index is
405        computed using the dose images from `self.dose1` and `self.dose2`,
406        along with specified dose percent and distance thresholds.
407        The resulting gamma index is stored in `self.gamma_index`, and the
408        pass ratio (the fraction of points with a gamma index less than or
409        equal to 1) is stored in `self.gamma_pass_ratio`.
410
411        ### Note:
412            Computing the gamma index may take some time.
413
414        ### Attributes:
415            self.gamma_index (BrachyDose): A BrachyDose object with the computed
416                gamma index.
417            self.gamma_pass_ratio (float): The ratio of points with a gamma index
418                less than or equal to 1.
419
420        ### Raises:
421            Any exceptions raised by the `gammaIndex` function or numpy operations
422            will propagate up to the caller.
423        """
424        self.gamma_index = BrachyDose.dose_with_empty_grid_like(self.dose1)
425        print("Computing gamma index may take time")
426        logger = logging.getLogger()
427        logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
428        self.gamma_index.dose_image = gammaIndex(
429            self.dose1.dose_image,
430            self.dose2.dose_image,
431            self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold,
432            self.gamma_distance_threshold,
433            **self.gamma_kwargs,
434        )
435        logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
436        self.gamma_index.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose_mask.dose_image.imageArray < 0] = np.nan
437        # cast the NaNs to 0s
438        gamma_index_grid = self.gamma_index.dose_image.imageArray
439        number_excluded = np.sum(np.isnan(gamma_index_grid))
440        gamma_index_grid[np.isnan(gamma_index_grid)] = -1
441        self.gamma_pass_ratio = (np.sum(gamma_index_grid <= 1) - number_excluded) / (
442            gamma_index_grid.size - number_excluded
443        )
444    
445    def write_percent_difference_to_nrrd(self, dir: str = "./"):
446        """
447        ### Purpose:
448        - Write the local and global percent difference to an NRRD file.
449
450        ### Inputs:
451        - path (str): The path where the NRRD file will be saved.
452
453        ### Outputs:
454        - None
455        """
456        if self.percent_difference_local is not None and self.percent_difference_global is not None:
457            self.percent_difference_local.write_to_nrrd(Path(f"{dir}/local_percent_difference.seq.nrrd"))
458            self.percent_difference_global.write_to_nrrd(Path(f"{dir}/global_percent_difference.seq.nrrd"))
459        else:
460            raise ValueError("Local/global difference not computed. Call compute_percent_difference() first.")
461    
462    def save_comparison_object(self, path: str = None):
463        r"""
464        ### Purpose:
465        - Saves the dose comparison object to a file using the pickle module.
466
467        ### Inputs:
468        - path (str): The path where the comparison object will be saved.
469
470        ### Returns:
471        - None
472        """
473        if not isinstance(path, str):
474            root = tk.Tk()
475            root.withdraw()
476            f = fd.asksaveasfile(
477                mode="wb",
478                defaultextension=".comp",
479                initialdir=os.getcwd(),
480                title="Save dose comparison object",
481                confirmoverwrite=True,
482            )
483            pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
484            root.destroy()
485            f.close()
486        else:
487            with open(path, "wb") as f:
488                pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)

490    def load_comparison_object(self, path: str = None):
491        r"""
492        ### Purpose:
493        - Opens the dose comparison object file and updates the current object's attributes with the loaded object's attributes.
494
495        ### Inputs:
496        - path (str): The path to the saved dose comparison object file.
497
498        ### Returns:
499        - None
500        """
501        if not isinstance(path, str):
502            root = tk.Tk()
503            root.withdraw()
504            f = fd.askopenfile(
505                mode="rb",
506                parent=root,
507                initialdir="$HOME",
508                title="Select saved dose comparison file",
509            )
510            self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)
511            # print(calibration_object_file_path)
512            root.destroy()
513            f.close()
514        else:
515            with open(path, "rb") as f:
516                self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)

532        """

555        matplotlib.rcParams.update({"font.size": 8})

749    def compute_dose_ratios(self):
750        """
751        ### Purpose:
752        - Compute the ratio between two dose distributions.
753        self.dose1 is the reference and self.dose2 is the test dose.
754
755        ### Outputs:
756        - None
757        """
758        self.dose_ratio = BrachyDose.dose_with_empty_grid_like(self.dose1)
759        self.dose_ratio.dose_image.imageArray = self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray / self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
760

Purpose:

  • A class to compare two BrachyDose objects by computing the percent difference and gamma index.

Attributes:

  • gamma_kwargs (dict): Keyword arguments for the pymedphys gamma index function. Please see pymedphys.gamma for more details
  • dose1 (BrachyDose): The first BrachyDose object (reference).
  • dose2 (BrachyDose): The second BrachyDose object (test), to resampled on the grid of dose1 with extrapolated points set to 0.
  • voxel_centers (np.ndarray): The voxel centers of the dose grid.
  • dose_2_grid_resampled (np.ndarray): The dose grid of dose2 resampled to the grid of dose1.
  • percent_difference (BrachyDose): The percent difference between dose1 and dose2.
  • gamma_index (BrachyDose): The gamma index between dose1 and dose2.
  • gamma_dose_percent_threshold (float): The gamma dose percent threshold.
  • gamma_distance_threshold (float): The gamma distance threshold in mm.
  • gamma_kwargs (dict): The kwargs for the gamma index function.
  • prescription_dose (float): The prescription dose of the dose grid.
  • max_gamma (float): The maximum gamma index value.
  • gamma_pass_ratio (float): The ratio of gamma index values passing the threshold.

 77        r"""
 78        ### Purpose:
 79        - to compare two BrachyDose objects. The comparison is done by computing the percent difference and gamma index.
 80        The gamma index is computed using the pymedphys gamma function. The result of the comparison is stored in the object and
 81        can be viewed using the plot_2d_dose_comparison function.
 82
 83        ### Inputs:
 84        - dose1: BrachyDose object
 85        - dose2: BrachyDose object
 86        - gamma_dose_percent_threshold: float := the gamma dose percent threshold
 87        - gamma_distance_threshold_mm: float := the gamma distance threshold in mm
 88        - compute_percent_difference: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed
 89        - compute_gamma_index: bool := if True, the gamma index will be computed
 90        - prescription_dose: float := the prescription dose of the dose grid
 91        - max_gamma: float := the maximum gamma index value
 92        - path: str := the path to the comparison object
 93        - gamma_kwargs: dict := the kwargs for the gamma index function
 94        - positive_percent_difference: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed with or without absolute value
 95        - percent_difference_range: tuple := the range of the percent difference used in plotting
 96        - dose_mask: BrachyDose := a mask to apply to the dose comparison, excluding any voxels where the mask is valued <0
 97
 98        ### Outputs:
 99        Object containing the following attributes:
100        - dose1: BrachyDose object
101        - dose2: BrachyDose object, resampled on the grid of dose1 with extrapolated
102            points set to 0
103        - voxel_centers: numpy array := the voxel centers of the dose grid
104        - dose_2_grid_resampled: numpy array := the dose grid of dose2 resampled to the grid of dose1
105        - percent_difference: BrachyDose object := the percent difference between dose1 and dose2
106        - gamma_index: BrachyDose object := the gamma index between dose1 and dose2
107        - gamma_dose_percent_threshold: float := the gamma dose percent threshold
108        - gamma_distance_threshold: float := the gamma distance threshold in mm
109        - gamma_kwargs: dict := the kwargs for the gamma index function
110        - plot_max_dose_percent_of_prescription : int = default 300%, can be tuned to get a good dynamic range for plots
111        and The following functions:
112            - compute_percent_difference: void := to compute the percent difference between dose1 and dose2
113            - compute_gamma_index: void := to compute the gamma index between dose1 and dose2
114            - plot_2d_dose_comparison: void := to plot the 2d dose comparison
115            - save_comparison_object
116            - load_comparison_object
117        """
118        # note: we will not use DoseComparisonImageProvider from OpenTPS
119        # since the gamma index capabilities are not yet implemented
120        # provide no dose to just load a file
121        if dose1 is None and dose2 is None:
122            self.load_comparison_object(path)
123            return
124
125        self.dose1 = dose1
126        self.dose2 = dose2
127        # axis is taken from the first dose provided
128        self.voxel_centers = dose1.get_voxel_centers()
129        # print("Before resample", self.dose2.dose_image is None)
130        self.dose2.dose_image.resampleOn(dose1.dose_image, fillValue=0)
131        # print("After resample", self.dose2.dose_image is None)
132        self.percent_difference_local: BrachyDose = None
133        self.percent_difference_global: BrachyDose = None
134        self.dose_ratio: BrachyDose = None
135        # self.dose_comparision_image_provider = DoseComparisonImageProvider()
136        self.gamma_index: BrachyDose = None
137        self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold = gamma_dose_percent_threshold
138        self.gamma_kwargs = BrachyDoseComparison.default_gamma_kwargs
139        self.gamma_kwargs.update(gamma_kwargs) #in case the user wants to change the default
140        self.plot_max_dose_percent_of_prescription : int = 200
141        self.prescription_dose = (
142            gamma_kwargs.get("global_normalisation", 1.0) 
143            if prescription_dose is None 
144            else prescription_dose
145            )
146        self.gamma_kwargs["global_normalisation"] = self.prescription_dose
147        self.max_gamma = gamma_kwargs.get("max_gamma", 1.1)
148        self.percent_difference_range = percent_difference_range
149        self.dose_mask = dose_mask if dose_mask is not None else BrachyDose.dose_with_ones_grid_like(self.dose1)
150        # axes values are assumed in cm from the 3ddose formalism
151        # gamma distance thresholds are usually provided in mm
152        # pymedphys documentation indicates that the threshold unit must match the axis
153        # despite the name of the function input containing 'mm'
154        self.gamma_distance_threshold = gamma_distance_threshold_mm
155        if compute_percent_difference:
156            self.compute_percent_difference(positive_percent_difference, local = True)
157            self.compute_percent_difference(positive_percent_difference, local = False)
158        if compute_gamma_index:
159            self.compute_gamma_index()
160        if compute_dose_ratios:
161            self.compute_dose_ratios()

def plot_2d_dose_comparison( self, axis_1_coords: numpy.ndarray, axis_2_coords: numpy.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str, plot_titles: tuple): 
163    def plot_2d_dose_comparison(
164        self,
165        axis_1_coords: np.ndarray,
166        axis_2_coords: np.ndarray,
167        plane_coord: float,
168        plane: str,
169        plot_titles: tuple,
170    ):
171        """
172        ### Purpose:
173        - Plots a 2D dose comparison between two dose profiles, along with their percent difference and gamma index.
174
175        ### Inputs:
176        - axis_1_coords : np.ndarray := Coordinates along the first axis (e.g., x-axis).
177        - axis_2_coords : np.ndarray := Coordinates along the second axis (e.g., y-axis).
178        - plane_coord : float := Coordinate of the plane in which the profiles are extracted.
179        - plane : str := The plane in which the profiles are extracted (e.g., 'axial', 'sagittal', 'coronal').
180        - plot_titles : tuple := Titles for the dose plots (dose 1 and dose 2).
181
182        ### Raises:
183        - NotImplementedError := If neither percent difference nor gamma index is computed.
184
185        ### Notes:
186        - The function generates a figure suitable for a double column figure in medical physics publications.
187        - The figure is saved as an EPS file (user is prompted for the filename) and displayed.
188        """
189
190        # import itertools
191
192        import matplotlib
193
194        # from matplotlib.ticker import (
195        # AutoMinorLocator,
196        # FormatStrFormatter,
197        # MultipleLocator,
198        # )
199
200        plot_vmax = self.plot_max_dose_percent_of_prescription / 100 * self.prescription_dose
201        matplotlib.rcParams.update({"font.size": 8})
202        plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 300})
203
204        figure_colormap = plt.get_cmap("turbo")
205        figure_colormap.set_bad(color="black", alpha=1.0)  # set bad values to black
206    
207
208        dummy_profile = np.zeros((len(axis_2_coords) - 1, len(axis_1_coords) - 1))
209
210        dose_1_profile = self.dose1.extract_profile_2d(
211            axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane
212        )
213        dose_2_profile = self.dose2.extract_profile_2d(
214            axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane
215        )
216        if self.percent_difference_local is not None:
217            percent_difference_profile = self.percent_difference_local.extract_profile_2d(
218                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane
219            )
220        else:
221            percent_difference_profile = dummy_profile
222        if self.gamma_index is not None:
223            gamma_index_profile = self.gamma_index.extract_profile_2d(
224                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane
225            )
226        else:
227            gamma_index_profile = dummy_profile
228
229        if self.dose_mask is not None:
230            dose_mask_profile = self.dose_mask.extract_profile_2d(
231                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane
232            )
233            dose_1_profile[dose_mask_profile < 0] = np.nan
234            dose_2_profile[dose_mask_profile < 0] = np.nan
235            percent_difference_profile[dose_mask_profile < 0] = np.nan
236            gamma_index_profile[dose_mask_profile < 0] = np.nan
237
238
239        #flip the profiles 
240        if plane == 'xy':
241            dose_1_profile = np.flip(dose_1_profile, axis=0)
242            dose_2_profile = np.flip(dose_2_profile, axis=0)
243            percent_difference_profile = np.flip(percent_difference_profile, axis=0)
244            gamma_index_profile = np.flip(gamma_index_profile, axis=0)
245
246
247        # elif self.gamma_index is :
248        #    raise NotImplementedError(
249        #        """Plotting of a comparison without computing the percent difference or
250        #    gamma index is not supported"""
251        #    )
252        # we will plot a figure that is suitable as a double column figure for medical physics
253        mm = 1.0 / 25.4  # define millimeters (relative to inches=1)
254        fig, ax = plt.subplots(
255            figsize=(180 * mm, 150 * mm), nrows=2, ncols=2, sharex=True, sharey=True
256        )
257        c00 = ax[0, 0].pcolormesh(
258            axis_1_coords,
259            axis_2_coords,
260            dose_1_profile,
261            vmin=0,
262            vmax=plot_vmax,
263            cmap=figure_colormap,
264            rasterized=True,
265            antialiased=True,
266        )
267        ax[0, 0].set_title(plot_titles[0], fontsize=12, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
268        ax[0, 0].set_aspect("equal")
269        cbar00 = fig.colorbar(c00, ax=ax[0, 0], shrink=0.9, pad=0.04)
270        cbar00.set_label(label="Dose [Gy]", size=10, labelpad=5)
271        # cbar00.mappable.set_clim(0, max_dose)
272        ax[0, 0].invert_yaxis()
273        ax[0, 0].set_ylabel(f"{plane[1]} [mm]", fontsize=10)
274        c01 = ax[0, 1].pcolormesh(
275            axis_1_coords,
276            axis_2_coords,
277            dose_2_profile,
278            vmin=0,
279            vmax=plot_vmax,
280            cmap=figure_colormap,
281            rasterized=True,
282            antialiased=True,
283        )
284        ax[0, 1].set_title(plot_titles[1], fontsize=12, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
285        ax[0, 1].set_aspect("equal")
286
287        cbar01 = fig.colorbar(c01, ax=ax[0, 1], shrink=0.9, pad=0.04)
288        cbar01.set_label(label="Dose [Gy]", size=10, labelpad=5)
289        # cbar01.mappable.set_clim(0, max_dose)g
290        ax[0, 1].invert_yaxis()
291        c10 = ax[1, 0].pcolormesh(
292            axis_1_coords,
293            axis_2_coords,
294            percent_difference_profile,
295            vmin=self.percent_difference_range[0],
296            vmax=self.percent_difference_range[1],
297            cmap=figure_colormap,
298            rasterized=True,
299            antialiased=True,
300        )
301        ax[1, 0].set_title("Percent Difference", fontsize=12, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
302        ax[1, 0].set_aspect("equal")
303        cbar10 = fig.colorbar(c10, ax=ax[1, 0], shrink=0.9, pad=0.04)
304        cbar10.set_label(label="[%]", size=10, labelpad=5)
305        ax[1, 0].invert_yaxis()
306        ax[1, 0].set_xlabel(f"{plane[0]} [mm]", fontsize=10)
307        ax[1, 0].set_ylabel(f"{plane[1]} [mm]", fontsize=10)
308
309        c11 = ax[1, 1].pcolormesh(
310            axis_1_coords,
311            axis_2_coords,
312            gamma_index_profile,
313            vmin=0,
314            vmax=self.max_gamma,
315            cmap=figure_colormap,
316            rasterized=True,
317            antialiased=True,
318        )
319        ax[1, 1].set_title(
320            f"Gamma ({self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold}% / {int(self.gamma_distance_threshold)} mm)",
321            fontsize=12,
322            pad=5,
323            fontweight="bold",
324        )
325        ax[1, 1].set_aspect("equal")
326        #: Pass Rate = {np.round(self.gamma_pass_ratio*100,1)}%"
327        cbar11 = fig.colorbar(c11, ax=ax[1, 1], shrink=0.9, pad=0.04)
328        cbar11.set_label(label="Gamma", size=10, labelpad=5)
329        ax[1, 1].invert_yaxis()
330        ax[1, 1].set_xlabel(f"{plane[0]} [mm]", fontsize=10)
331        plt.tight_layout()
332        plt.show()
333
334        root = tk.Tk()
335        root.withdraw()
336        f = fd.asksaveasfile(
337            mode="wb",
338            defaultextension=".eps",
339            initialdir=os.getcwd(),
340            title="Save dose comparison plots",
341            confirmoverwrite=True,
342        )
343        if f is not None:
344            plt.savefig(f, dpi=300)
345            f.close()
346
347        root.destroy()

Inputs:

  • axis_1_coords : np.ndarray := Coordinates along the first axis (e.g., x-axis).
  • axis_2_coords : np.ndarray := Coordinates along the second axis (e.g., y-axis).
  • plane_coord : float := Coordinate of the plane in which the profiles are extracted.
  • plane : str := The plane in which the profiles are extracted (e.g., 'axial', 'sagittal', 'coronal').
  • plot_titles : tuple := Titles for the dose plots (dose 1 and dose 2).

Raises:

def compute_percent_difference(self, positive_percent_difference: bool = True, local: bool = True): 
349    def compute_percent_difference(self, positive_percent_difference: bool = True, local: bool = True):
350        """
351        ### Purpose:
352        - Compute the local or global percent difference between two dose distributions.
353        self.dose1 is the reference and self.dose2 is the test dose.
354        See TG-372 for exact definitions
355        
356        ### Inputs:
357        - positive_percent_difference: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed with or without
358        absolute value
359        - local: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed locally; otherwise globally
360
361        ### Outputs:
362        - None. but updates the following attributes of the object:
363        - percent_difference_local: BrachyDose object := the local percent difference between dose1 and dose2
364        - percent_difference_global: BrachyDose object := the global percent difference between dose1 and dose2
365        """
366        #make sure there's no 0s in the ref dose to prevent division by 0
367        self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray == 0] = 1e-6 
368        if local:
369            self.percent_difference_local = BrachyDose.dose_with_empty_grid_like(self.dose1)
370            if positive_percent_difference:
371                self.percent_difference_local.dose_image.imageArray = (
372                    np.abs(self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray)
373                    / self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
374                    * 100.0
375                )
376            else:
377                self.percent_difference_local.dose_image.imageArray = (
378                    self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
379                ) * 100.0 / self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
380            if self.dose_mask is not None:
381                self.percent_difference_local.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose_mask.dose_image.imageArray < 0] = np.nan
382
383        else:
384            self.percent_difference_global = BrachyDose.dose_with_empty_grid_like(self.dose1)
385            if positive_percent_difference:
386                self.percent_difference_global.dose_image.imageArray = (
387                    np.abs(self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray)
388                    / self.prescription_dose
389                    * 100.0
390                )
391            else:
392                self.percent_difference_global.dose_image.imageArray = (
393                    self.dose2.dose_image.imageArray - self.dose1.dose_image.imageArray
394                ) * 100.0 / self.prescription_dose
395
396            if self.dose_mask is not None:
397                self.percent_difference_global.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose_mask.dose_image.imageArray < 0] = np.nan

Purpose:

  • Compute the local or global percent difference between two dose distributions. self.dose1 is the reference and self.dose2 is the test dose. See TG-372 for exact definitions

Inputs:

  • positive_percent_difference: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed with or without absolute value
  • local: bool := if True, the percent difference will be computed locally; otherwise globally

Outputs:

  • None. but updates the following attributes of the object:
  • percent_difference_local: BrachyDose object := the local percent difference between dose1 and dose2
  • percent_difference_global: BrachyDose object := the global percent difference between dose1 and dose2
def compute_gamma_index(self): 
399    def compute_gamma_index(self):
400        """
401        ### Purpose:
402        - Compute the gamma index between two dose distributions.
403        This method calculates the gamma index, which is a quantitative measure
404        of the agreement between two dose distributions. The gamma index is
405        computed using the dose images from `self.dose1` and `self.dose2`,
406        along with specified dose percent and distance thresholds.
407        The resulting gamma index is stored in `self.gamma_index`, and the
408        pass ratio (the fraction of points with a gamma index less than or
409        equal to 1) is stored in `self.gamma_pass_ratio`.
410
411        ### Note:
412            Computing the gamma index may take some time.
413
414        ### Attributes:
415            self.gamma_index (BrachyDose): A BrachyDose object with the computed
416                gamma index.
417            self.gamma_pass_ratio (float): The ratio of points with a gamma index
418                less than or equal to 1.
419
420        ### Raises:
421            Any exceptions raised by the `gammaIndex` function or numpy operations
422            will propagate up to the caller.
423        """
424        self.gamma_index = BrachyDose.dose_with_empty_grid_like(self.dose1)
425        print("Computing gamma index may take time")
426        logger = logging.getLogger()
427        logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
428        self.gamma_index.dose_image = gammaIndex(
429            self.dose1.dose_image,
430            self.dose2.dose_image,
431            self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold,
432            self.gamma_distance_threshold,
433            **self.gamma_kwargs,
434        )
435        logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
436        self.gamma_index.dose_image.imageArray[self.dose_mask.dose_image.imageArray < 0] = np.nan
437        # cast the NaNs to 0s
438        gamma_index_grid = self.gamma_index.dose_image.imageArray
439        number_excluded = np.sum(np.isnan(gamma_index_grid))
440        gamma_index_grid[np.isnan(gamma_index_grid)] = -1
441        self.gamma_pass_ratio = (np.sum(gamma_index_grid <= 1) - number_excluded) / (
442            gamma_index_grid.size - number_excluded
443        )

Purpose:

  • Compute the gamma index between two dose distributions. This method calculates the gamma index, which is a quantitative measure of the agreement between two dose distributions. The gamma index is computed using the dose images from self.dose1 and self.dose2, along with specified dose percent and distance thresholds. The resulting gamma index is stored in self.gamma_index, and the pass ratio (the fraction of points with a gamma index less than or equal to 1) is stored in self.gamma_pass_ratio.

Note:

Computing the gamma index may take some time.

Attributes:

self.gamma_index (BrachyDose): A BrachyDose object with the computed
    gamma index.
self.gamma_pass_ratio (float): The ratio of points with a gamma index
    less than or equal to 1.

Raises:

Any exceptions raised by the `gammaIndex` function or numpy operations
will propagate up to the caller.

def save_comparison_object(self, path: str = None): 
462    def save_comparison_object(self, path: str = None):
463        r"""
464        ### Purpose:
465        - Saves the dose comparison object to a file using the pickle module.
466
467        ### Inputs:
468        - path (str): The path where the comparison object will be saved.
469
470        ### Returns:
471        - None
472        """
473        if not isinstance(path, str):
474            root = tk.Tk()
475            root.withdraw()
476            f = fd.asksaveasfile(
477                mode="wb",
478                defaultextension=".comp",
479                initialdir=os.getcwd(),
480                title="Save dose comparison object",
481                confirmoverwrite=True,
482            )
483            pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
484            root.destroy()
485            f.close()
486        else:
487            with open(path, "wb") as f:
488                pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)

def load_comparison_object(self, path: str = None): 
490    def load_comparison_object(self, path: str = None):
491        r"""
492        ### Purpose:
493        - Opens the dose comparison object file and updates the current object's attributes with the loaded object's attributes.
494
495        ### Inputs:
496        - path (str): The path to the saved dose comparison object file.
497
498        ### Returns:
499        - None
500        """
501        if not isinstance(path, str):
502            root = tk.Tk()
503            root.withdraw()
504            f = fd.askopenfile(
505                mode="rb",
506                parent=root,
507                initialdir="$HOME",
508                title="Select saved dose comparison file",
509            )
510            self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)
511            # print(calibration_object_file_path)
512            root.destroy()
513            f.close()
514        else:
515            with open(path, "rb") as f:
516                self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)

750        """
751        ### Purpose:

class CalibrationCurve: 
 29class CalibrationCurve:
 30    """
 31    A class used to represent a calibration curve for film dosimetry.
 32
 33    Attributes:
 34    - doses (numpy.ndarray): doses used to create calibration curve
 35    - r_pv (numpy.ndarray): red channel pixel values on calibration films
 36    - g_pv (numpy.ndarray): green channel pixel values
 37    - b_pv (numpy.ndarray): blue channel pixel values
 38    - r_std (numpy.ndarray): standard deviation of red channel pixel values
 39    - g_std (numpy.ndarray): standard deviation of green channel pixel values
 40    - b_std (numpy.ndarray): standard deviation of blue channel pixel values
 41    - calibration_curve_type (str): type of calibration curve
 42    - r_opt (numpy.ndarray): optimal parameters for red channel calibration curve
 43    - g_opt (numpy.ndarray): optimal parameters for green channel calibration curve
 44    - b_opt (numpy.ndarray): optimal parameters for blue channel calibration curve
 45    - rp_cov (numpy.ndarray): covariance matrix for red channel fit
 46    - gp_cov (numpy.ndarray): covariance matrix for green channel fit
 47    - bp_cov (numpy.ndarray): covariance matrix for blue channel fit
 48    - dose_to_pv (function): function to convert dose to pixel value
 49    - pv_to_dose (function): function to convert pixel value to dose
 50    - r_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): red channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value
 51    - g_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): green channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value
 52    - b_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): blue channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value (for Lewis) or net pixel value (for Devic)
 53
 54    Methods:
 55    - perform_fit(): performs the fit for the calibration curve
 56    - define_fit_parameters_for_calibration_type(): defines the fit parameters for the calibration type based on the calibration curve type
 57    - plot_calibration_and_response_curve(): plots the calibration and response curves for the film dosimetry system
 58    """
 59
 60    def __init__(
 61        self, doses, r_pv, g_pv, b_pv, r_std, g_std, b_std, calibration_curve_type
 62    ):
 63        self.doses: np.array = doses  # doses used to create calibration curve
 64        self.r_pv: np.array = r_pv  # red channel pixel values on calibration films
 65        self.g_pv: np.array = g_pv  # green channel pixel values
 66        self.b_pv: np.array = b_pv  # blue channel pixel values
 67        self.r_std: np.array = r_std  # standard deviation of red channel pixel values
 68        self.g_std: np.array = g_std  # standard deviation of green channel pixel values
 69        self.b_std: np.array = b_std  # standard deviation of blue channel pixel values
 70        self.calibration_curve_type = (
 71            calibration_curve_type  # type of calibration curve
 72        )
 73        self.r_opt: np.array = (
 74            None  # optimal parameters for red channel calibration curve
 75        )
 76        self.g_opt: np.array = (
 77            None  # optimal parameters for green channel calibration curve
 78        )
 79        self.b_opt: np.array = (
 80            None  # optimal parameters for blue channel calibration curve
 81        )
 82        self.rp_cov: np.array = None  # covariance matrix for red channel fit
 83        self.gp_cov: np.array = None  # covariance matrix for green channel fit
 84        self.bp_cov: np.array = None  # covariance matrix for blue channel fit
 85        self.dose_to_pv = None  # function to convert dose to pixel value
 86        self.pv_to_dose = None  # function to convert pixel value to dose
 87        self.r_pv_fit: np.array = (
 88            None  # mean red channel pixel values to fit; normalized to the zero dose pixel value
 89        )
 90        self.g_pv_fit: np.array = (
 91            None  # mean green channel pixel values to fit; normalized to the zero dose pixel value
 92        )
 93        self.b_pv_fit: np.array = (
 94            None  # mean blue channel pixel values to fit; normalized to the zero dose pixel value
 95        )
 96        self.define_fit_parameters_for_calibration_type()
 97        self.perform_fit()
 98        # don't plot if running under a tester
 99        if "PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST" not in os.environ:
100            self.plot_calibration_and_response_curve()
101
102    def perform_fit(self):
103        """
104        Perform curve fitting to obtain optimal parameters and covariance matrices for red, green, and blue channels.
105
106        Returns:
107        - r_opt: array_like
108        Optimal parameters for red channel.
109        - rp_cov: 2-D array
110        Covariance matrix for the estimated parameters for red channel.
111        - g_opt: array_like
112        Optimal parameters for green channel.
113        - gp_cov: 2-D array
114        Covariance matrix for the estimated parameters for green channel.
115        - b_opt: array_like
116        Optimal parameters for blue channel.
117        - bp_cov: 2-D array
118        Covariance matrix for the estimated parameters for blue channel.
119        """
120        self.r_opt, self.rp_cov = curve_fit(
121            self.dose_to_pv, self.doses, self.r_pv_fit, sigma=self.r_std
122        )
123        self.g_opt, self.gp_cov = curve_fit(
124            self.dose_to_pv, self.doses, self.g_pv_fit, sigma=self.g_std
125        )
126        self.b_opt, self.bp_cov = curve_fit(
127            self.dose_to_pv, self.doses, self.b_pv_fit, sigma=self.b_std
128        )
129
130    def define_fit_parameters_for_calibration_type(self):
131        """
132        Defines the fit parameters for the calibration type based on the calibration curve type.
133
134        Args:
135        - doses (numpy.ndarray): Array of doses
136        - r_pv (numpy.ndarray): Array of red channel pixel values
137        - g_pv (numpy.ndarray): Array of green channel pixel values
138        - b_pv (numpy.ndarray): Array of blue channel pixel values
139
140        Returns:
141        - Tuple containing:
142        - dose_to_pv (function): Function to convert dose to pixel value
143        - pv_to_dose (function): Function to convert pixel value to dose
144        - r_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): Array of red channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value
145        - g_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): Array of green channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value
146        - b_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): Array of blue channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value (for Lewis) or net pixel value (for Devic)
147        """
148        if self.calibration_curve_type == "Lewis":
149            self.dose_to_pv = FilmCalibration.lewis_dose_to_pv
150            self.pv_to_dose = FilmCalibration.lewis_pv_to_dose
151            # normalize to the zero dose pv for Lewis
152            # print(r_pv, doses==0)
153            self.r_pv_fit = self.r_pv / (self.r_pv[self.doses == 0])
154            self.g_pv_fit = self.g_pv / (self.g_pv[self.doses == 0])
155            self.b_pv_fit = self.b_pv / (self.b_pv[self.doses == 0])
156
157        elif self.calibration_curve_type == "Devic":
158            self.dose_to_pv = FilmCalibration.devic_dose_to_pv
159            self.pv_to_dose = FilmCalibration.devic_pv_to_dose
160            # Devic uses net pvs
161            self.r_pv_fit = np.abs(np.array(self.r_pv) - self.r_pv[self.doses == 0])
162            self.g_pv_fit = np.abs(np.array(self.g_pv) - self.g_pv[self.doses == 0])
163            self.b_pv_fit = np.abs(np.array(self.b_pv) - self.b_pv[self.doses == 0])
164
165    def plot_calibration_and_response_curve(self):
166        """
167        Plots the calibration and response curves for the film dosimetry system.
168        The calibration curve relates the measured pixel values (PV) to the actual
169        radiation dose delivered to the film. The response curve relates the
170        normalized PV to the actual radiation dose delivered to the film.
171        """
172
173        # doses = self.calibration_curve_params['doses']
174        # r_pv = self.calibration_curve_params['r_pv']
175        # g_pv = self.calibration_curve_params['g_pv']
176        # b_pv = self.calibration_curve_params['b_pv']
177        # r_opt = self.calibration_curve_params['r_opt']
178        # g_opt = self.calibration_curve_params['g_opt']
179        # b_opt = self.calibration_curve_params['b_opt']
180
181        fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, dpi=150, sharex=True)
182        # Remove space so awesome sharex visual
183        fig.subplots_adjust(hspace=0.03)
184        ax[0].plot(self.doses, self.r_pv, "r", label="Red")
185        ax[0].plot(self.doses, self.g_pv, "g", label="Green")
186        ax[0].plot(self.doses, self.b_pv, "b", label="Blue")
187        yl1 = ax[0].set_ylabel("PV", labelpad=25)
188        yl1.set_rotation(0)
189        ax[0].grid()
190        ax[0].legend()
191
192        # Plot derivative to highlight usable ranges per channel
193        d_dose = (np.array(self.doses)[:-1] + np.array(self.doses)[1:]) / 2
194        d_r_pv = np.diff(self.r_pv) / np.diff(self.doses)
195        d_g_pv = np.diff(self.g_pv) / np.diff(self.doses)
196        d_b_pv = np.diff(self.b_pv) / np.diff(self.doses)
197        ax[1].plot(d_dose, -d_r_pv, "r", label="Red")
198        ax[1].plot(d_dose, -d_g_pv, "g", label="Green")
199        ax[1].plot(d_dose, -d_b_pv, "b", label="Blue")
200        ax[1].set_xlabel("Dose (Gy)")
201        yl2 = ax[1].set_ylabel(r"$-\frac{\partial{PV}}{\partial Dose}$", labelpad=25)
202        yl2.set_rotation(0)
203        ax[1].set_yscale("log")
204        ax[1].grid()
205        ax[1].legend()
206
207        dose_array = np.linspace(0, 40, 100)
208        r_pv_array = np.linspace(0.12, 1, 100)
209        g_pv_array = np.linspace(0.15, 1, 100)
210        b_pv_array = np.linspace(0.30, 1, 100)
211
212        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, dpi=150, figsize=(20, 5))
213
214        legend_elements = [
215            Line2D(
216                [0],
217                [0],
218                marker=".",
219                markersize=10,
220                markerfacecolor="black",
221                color="w",
222                label="Experiment",
223            ),
224            Line2D([0], [0], color="black", label="Fit"),
225        ]
226
227        # Response Curve
228        ax[0].plot(self.doses, self.r_pv_fit, "r.")
229        ax[0].plot(self.doses, self.g_pv_fit, "g.")
230        ax[0].plot(self.doses, self.b_pv_fit, "b.")
231
232        ax[0].plot(
233            dose_array, self.dose_to_pv(dose_array, *self.r_opt), "r", label="Red fit"
234        )
235        ax[0].plot(
236            dose_array, self.dose_to_pv(dose_array, *self.g_opt), "g", label="Green fit"
237        )
238        ax[0].plot(
239            dose_array, self.dose_to_pv(dose_array, *self.b_opt), "b", label="Blue fit"
240        )
241
242        ax[0].grid()
243        ax[0].set_xlabel("Dose (Gy)")
244        ax[0].set_ylabel("Normalized PV")
245        ax[0].legend(loc="best", handles=legend_elements)
246        ax[0].set_title("Response Curve")
247
248        # Calibration Curve
249        ax[1].plot(self.r_pv_fit, self.doses, "r.")
250        ax[1].plot(self.g_pv_fit, self.doses, "g.")
251        ax[1].plot(self.b_pv_fit, self.doses, "b.")
252
253        ax[1].plot(r_pv_array, self.pv_to_dose(r_pv_array, *self.r_opt), "r")
254        ax[1].plot(g_pv_array, self.pv_to_dose(g_pv_array, *self.g_opt), "g")
255        ax[1].plot(b_pv_array, self.pv_to_dose(b_pv_array, *self.b_opt), "b")
256
257        ax[1].grid()
258        ax[1].set_xlabel("Normalized PV")
259        ax[1].set_ylabel("Dose (Gy)")
260        ax[1].legend(loc="best", handles=legend_elements)
261        ax[1].set_title("Calibration Curve")
262
263        # Dose Residual Plot
264        ax[2].plot(
265            self.doses,
266            100
267            * (self.doses - self.pv_to_dose(self.r_pv_fit, *self.r_opt))
268            / self.doses,
269            "r.",
270        )
271        ax[2].plot(
272            self.doses,
273            100
274            * (self.doses - self.pv_to_dose(self.g_pv_fit, *self.g_opt))
275            / self.doses,
276            "g.",
277        )
278        ax[2].plot(
279            self.doses,
280            100
281            * (self.doses - self.pv_to_dose(self.b_pv_fit, *self.b_opt))
282            / self.doses,
283            "b.",
284        )
285
286        ax[2].axhline(-2, linestyle="--")
287        ax[2].axhline(2, linestyle="--")
288
289        ax[2].set_ylabel("Given Dose - Measured Dose (%)")
290        ax[2].set_xlabel("Dose (Gy)")
291        ax[2].grid()
292        ax[2].set_title("Dose Error")

A class used to represent a calibration curve for film dosimetry.

Attributes:

  • doses (numpy.ndarray): doses used to create calibration curve
  • r_pv (numpy.ndarray): red channel pixel values on calibration films
  • g_pv (numpy.ndarray): green channel pixel values
  • b_pv (numpy.ndarray): blue channel pixel values
  • r_std (numpy.ndarray): standard deviation of red channel pixel values
  • g_std (numpy.ndarray): standard deviation of green channel pixel values
  • b_std (numpy.ndarray): standard deviation of blue channel pixel values
  • calibration_curve_type (str): type of calibration curve
  • r_opt (numpy.ndarray): optimal parameters for red channel calibration curve
  • g_opt (numpy.ndarray): optimal parameters for green channel calibration curve
  • b_opt (numpy.ndarray): optimal parameters for blue channel calibration curve
  • rp_cov (numpy.ndarray): covariance matrix for red channel fit
  • gp_cov (numpy.ndarray): covariance matrix for green channel fit
  • bp_cov (numpy.ndarray): covariance matrix for blue channel fit
  • dose_to_pv (function): function to convert dose to pixel value
  • pv_to_dose (function): function to convert pixel value to dose
  • r_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): red channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value
  • g_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): green channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value
  • b_pv_fit (numpy.ndarray): blue channel pixel values normalized to the zero dose pixel value (for Lewis) or net pixel value (for Devic)

Methods:

  • perform_fit(): performs the fit for the calibration curve
  • define_fit_parameters_for_calibration_type(): defines the fit parameters for the calibration type based on the calibration curve type
  • plot_calibration_and_response_curve(): plots the calibration and response curves for the film dosimetry system

239            dose_array, self.dose_to_pv(dose_array, *self.b_opt), "b", label="Blue fit"
240        )
241
242        ax[0].grid()
243        ax[0].set_xlabel("Dose (Gy)")
244        ax[0].set_ylabel("Normalized PV")
245        ax[0].legend(loc="best", handles=legend_elements)
246        ax[0].set_title("Response Curve")
247
248        # Calibration Curve
249        ax[1].plot(self.r_pv_fit, self.doses, "r.")
250        ax[1].plot(self.g_pv_fit, self.doses, "g.")
251        ax[1].plot(self.b_pv_fit, self.doses, "b.")
252
253        ax[1].plot(r_pv_array, self.pv_to_dose(r_pv_array, *self.r_opt), "r")
254        ax[1].plot(g_pv_array, self.pv_to_dose(g_pv_array, *self.g_opt), "g")
255        ax[1].plot(b_pv_array, self.pv_to_dose(b_pv_array, *self.b_opt), "b")
256
257        ax[1].grid()
258        ax[1].set_xlabel("Normalized PV")
259        ax[1].set_ylabel("Dose (Gy)")
260        ax[1].legend(loc="best", handles=legend_elements)
261        ax[1].set_title("Calibration Curve")
262
263        # Dose Residual Plot
264        ax[2].plot(
265            self.doses,
266            100
267            * (self.doses - self.pv_to_dose(self.r_pv_fit, *self.r_opt))
268            / self.doses,
269            "r.",
270        )
271        ax[2].plot(
272            self.doses,
273            100
274            * (self.doses - self.pv_to_dose(self.g_pv_fit, *self.g_opt))
275            / self.doses,
276            "g.",
277        )
278        ax[2].plot(
279            self.doses,
280            100
281            * (self.doses - self.pv_to_dose(self.b_pv_fit, *self.b_opt))
282            / self.doses,
283            "b.",
284        )
285
286        ax[2].axhline(-2, linestyle="--")
287        ax[2].axhline(2, linestyle="--")
288
289        ax[2].set_ylabel("Given Dose - Measured Dose (%)")
290        ax[2].set_xlabel("Dose (Gy)")
291        ax[2].grid()
292        ax[2].set_title("Dose Error")

Plots the calibration and response curves for the film dosimetry system. The calibration curve relates the measured pixel values (PV) to the actual radiation dose delivered to the film. The response curve relates the normalized PV to the actual radiation dose delivered to the film.

295class FilmCalibration:
296    r"""
297    A utility class for processing film images in the context of brachytherapy.
298
299    This class provides methods for loading and processing calibration images, as well as for applying
300    calibration curves to film images. It also stores various parameters related to the calibration process,
301    such as the pixel range, the calibration file directory, and the ROI bounds.
302
303    Attributes:
304    pixel_range (int): The maximum pixel value for the film images.
305    calibration_file_dict (dict): A dictionary mapping dose values to calibration file paths and calibration
306    coefficients.
307    calibration_images (dict): A dictionary mapping dose values to calibration images.
308    calibration_curve_type (str): The type of calibration curve used to fit the calibration data.
309    calibration_curve_params (dict): A dictionary of parameters for the calibration curve.
310    film_to_mc_offset (tuple): The offset between the film and the Monte Carlo (MC) simulation.
311    roi_bounds (tuple): The bounds of the region of interest (ROI) for the film images.
312    calibration_file_directory (str): The directory where the calibration files are stored.
313    """
314
315    possible_calibrations = ["Lewis", "Devic"]
316
317    def __init__(self):
318        self.pixel_range: int = None
319        self.calibration_file_dict: dict = {}  # [float, tuple]
320        self.calibration_images: dict = {}  # [float, np.ndarray]
321        self.calibration_curve_type: str = None
322        self.calibration_curve: CalibrationCurve = None
323        self.film_to_mc_offset: tuple = None
324        self.roi_bounds: tuple = (100, 100, 150, 150)  # x1 y1 x2 y2
325        self.calibration_file_directory: str = "$HOME"

327    def configure_calibration(self):
328        r"""
329        Configures the calibration settings for the film.

334        Then loads and plots the calibration data.

336        while self.calibration_curve_type not in FilmCalibration.possible_calibrations:
337            print("Choose calibration curve type (Lewis or Devic):")
338            self.calibration_curve_type = input()
339        while not isinstance(self.pixel_range, int):
340            print(
341                "Enter the number of possible pixel values (e.g. 2^16 for 16 bit images):"
342            )

345                self.pixel_range = int(pixel_range_str)
346                print(pixel_range_str, self.pixel_range)
347            except ValueError:
348                print("Invalid input. Please enter an integer.")
349        print(
350            "Begin selecting calibration film files. Enter a dose and select the calibration films at that dose or enter 'Done' to finish."
351        )

353        while current_dose_str != "Done":
354            try:
355                current_dose = float(current_dose_str)
356                self.add_calibration_files_for_dose(current_dose)
357            except ValueError:
358                print("Invalid input. Please enter a float or 'Done' to finish.")
359            current_dose_str = input()

362    def add_calibration_files_for_dose(self, dose: float):
363        r"""Opens a file dialog to select calibration film files corresponding to a given dose.
364
365        Args:
366        dose (float): The dose in Gy for which to select calibration files.
367
368        Returns:
369        None
370
371        Side effects:
372        - Modifies the `calibration_file_dict` attribute of the object to include the selected files.
373        - Modifies the `calibration_file_directory` attribute of the object to the directory of the last selected file.
374        """
375        root = tk.Tk()
376        root.withdraw()
377        filenames_for_dose = fd.askopenfilenames(
378            parent=root,
379            initialdir=self.calibration_file_directory,

381            + str(dose)
382            + " Gy",
383        )
384        if len(filenames_for_dose) > 0:
385            # start navigation of directory of last selected file

387            self.calibration_file_dict[dose] = filenames_for_dose

390    def load_calibration(self):
391        r"""
392        Loads calibration images from a dictionary of file paths and calculates the mean pixel value for each image.
393
394        Raises:
395        ValueError: If the calibration file dictionary is not set.
396
397        Returns:
398        None
399        """
400        if self.calibration_file_dict is None:
401            raise ValueError("calibration file dictionary not set")
402        else:
403            self.calibration_images = {
404                j: np.mean(
405                    [tifffile.imread(i) for i in self.calibration_file_dict[j]], axis=0
406                )
407                / self.pixel_range
408                for j in self.calibration_file_dict.keys()
409            }

411    def display_calibration_films(self):

414        """

416            raise ValueError("calibration images not loaded")
417        else:
418            nplots = len(self.calibration_images.keys())
419            _, axes = plt.subplots(1, nplots, dpi=124, figsize=(15, 10), squeeze=True)
420            i = 0
421            if nplots == 1:
422                plt.imshow(
423                    self.calibration_images[list(self.calibration_images.keys())[i]][
424                        :, :, 0

428                plt.title(str(list(self.calibration_images.keys())[i]))
429                plt.axvline(self.roi_bounds[0], color="r")
430                plt.axhline(self.roi_bounds[1], color="r")
