432                plt.axhline(self.roi_bounds[3], color="r")
433            else:
434                for ax in axes.flatten():
435                    ax.imshow(
436                        self.calibration_images[
437                            list(self.calibration_images.keys())[i]
438                        ][:, :, 0],
439                        cmap="turbo",
440                    )
441                    ax.set_title(str(list(self.calibration_images.keys())[i]))
442                    ax.axvline(self.roi_bounds[0], color="r")
443                    ax.axhline(self.roi_bounds[1], color="r")
444                    ax.axvline(self.roi_bounds[2], color="r")
445                    ax.axhline(self.roi_bounds[3], color="r")
446                    i += 1
447
448    def set_roi_bounds(self, new_bounds: tuple):
449        r"""
450        Set the region of interest (ROI) bounds for the film.
451
452        Args:
453        new_bounds (tuple): A tuple of length 4 containing the x and y coordinates of the top-left corner of the ROI,
454        followed by the width and height of the ROI.
455
456        Raises:
457        ValueError: If the length of new_bounds is not 4 or if any element in new_bounds is not an integer.
458        """
459        if len(new_bounds) != 4:
460            raise ValueError("ROI bounds must be a tuple of length 4")
461        for i in new_bounds:
462            if not isinstance(i, int):
463                raise ValueError("ROI bounds must be a tuple of integers")
464        self.roi_bounds = new_bounds
465
466    def create_calibration_curve(self):
467        r"""
468        Create a calibration curve for a film dosimetry image.
469
470        The calibration curve is created by analyzing a set of calibration images
471        with known doses and calculating the mean pixel value in a region of
472        interest (ROI) for each color channel (red, green, blue) as a function of
473        dose. The calibration curve is then fitted to a response curve and a
474        calibration curve, which are plotted along with a dose residual plot.
475
476        Returns:
477        None
478        """
479        doses = np.array(list(self.calibration_images.keys()))
480        r_pv = np.array([])
481        g_pv = []
482        b_pv = []
483
484        r_std = []
485        g_std = []
486        b_std = []
487
488        # check that the ROI bounds are on the image, if not throw an error
489        for dose in doses:
490            print(dose, " ", self.calibration_images[dose].shape)
491            if (
492            self.roi_bounds[0] < 0
493            or self.roi_bounds[1] < 0
494            or self.roi_bounds[2] > self.calibration_images[dose].shape[1]
495            or self.roi_bounds[3] > self.calibration_images[dose].shape[0]
496            ):
497                raise ValueError(
498                    f"ROI bounds {self.roi_bounds} are outside the image with shape {self.calibration_images[dose].shape} at dose {dose}"
499                )
500
501        # populate arrays with mean pixel value in ROI as a function of dose
502        r_pv = np.array(
503            [
504                self.calibration_images[dose][
505                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
506                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
507                    0,
508                ].mean()
509                for dose in doses
510            ]
511        )
512        g_pv = np.array(
513            [
514                self.calibration_images[dose][
515                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
516                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
517                    1,
518                ].mean()
519                for dose in doses
520            ]
521        )
522        b_pv = np.array(
523            [
524                self.calibration_images[dose][
525                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
526                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
527                    2,
528                ].mean()
529                for dose in doses
530            ]
531        )
532
533        r_std = np.array(
534            [
535                self.calibration_images[dose][
536                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
537                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
538                    0,
539                ].std()
540                for dose in doses
541            ]
542        )
543        g_std = np.array(
544            [
545                self.calibration_images[dose][
546                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
547                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
548                    1,
549                ].std()
550                for dose in doses
551            ]
552        )
553        b_std = np.array(
554            [
555                self.calibration_images[dose][
556                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
557                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
558                    2,
559                ].std()
560                for dose in doses
561            ]
562        )
563
564        # print('red channel:', rstd)
565        # print('green channel:', gstd)
566        # print('blue channel:', bstd)
567        self.calibration_curve = CalibrationCurve(
568            doses, r_pv, g_pv, b_pv, r_std, g_std, b_std, self.calibration_curve_type
569        )
570
571    def normalize_image_by_calibration_type(self, image: np.array):
572        """
573        Normalizes the given image based on the calibration curve type.
574
575        Args:
576        - image: A numpy array representing the image to be normalized, with shape (height, width, 3).
577
578        Returns:
579        A tuple containing the pv_to_dose conversion function and the normalized image.
580
581        Throws:
582        ValueError: If the image does not have 3 channels.
583        """
584        if image.shape[2] != 3:
585            raise ValueError("Image must have 3 channels")
586        norm_image = np.zeros(image.shape)
587        doses = self.calibration_curve.doses
588        r_pv = self.calibration_curve.r_pv
589        g_pv = self.calibration_curve.g_pv
590        b_pv = self.calibration_curve.b_pv
591        if self.calibration_curve_type == "Lewis":
592            pv_to_dose = FilmCalibration.lewis_pv_to_dose
593            norm_image[:, :, 0] = image[:, :, 0] / r_pv[doses == 0]
594            norm_image[:, :, 1] = image[:, :, 1] / g_pv[doses == 0]
595            norm_image[:, :, 2] = image[:, :, 2] / b_pv[doses == 0]
596        elif self.calibration_curve_type == "Devic":
597            pv_to_dose = FilmCalibration.devic_pv_to_dose
598            norm_image[:, :, 0] = np.abs(image[:, :, 0] - r_pv[doses == 0])
599            norm_image[:, :, 1] = np.abs(image[:, :, 1] - g_pv[doses == 0])
600            norm_image[:, :, 2] = np.abs(image[:, :, 2] - b_pv[doses == 0])
601        else:
602            raise ValueError("Invalid calibration curve type")
603        return (pv_to_dose, norm_image)
604
605    @staticmethod
606    def lewis_dose_to_pv(d, a, b, c):
607        r"""
608        Calculates the PV value for a given dose using the Lewis model.
609
610        Args:
611        d (float): The dose value.
612        a (float): The a parameter of the Lewis model.
613        b (float): The b parameter of the Lewis model.
614        c (float): The c parameter of the Lewis model.
615
616        Returns:
617        float: The PV value calculated using the Lewis model.
618        """
619        return a + b / (d + c)
620
621    @staticmethod
622    def lewis_pv_to_dose(pv, a, b, c):
623        r"""
624        Converts a given PV value to a dose value using the Lewis formula.
625
626        Args:
627        pv (float): The PV value to convert to dose.
628        a (float): The 'a' parameter of the Lewis formula.
629        b (float): The 'b' parameter of the Lewis formula.
630        c (float): The 'c' parameter of the Lewis formula.
631
632        Returns:
633        float: The dose value corresponding to the given PV value.
634        """
635        return -c + b / (pv - a)
636
637    @staticmethod
638    def devic_pv_to_dose(pv, a, b):
639        r"""
640        Converts a pixel value (PV) to a dose value using the Devic formula.
641
642        Args:
643        pv (float): Pixel value
644        a (float): Calibration coefficient
645        b (float): Calibration coefficient
646
647        Returns:
648        float: Dose value
649        """
650        return (a * pv) / (1 - b * pv)
651
652    @staticmethod
653    def devic_dose_to_pv(d, a, b):
654        r"""
655        Converts a measured dose value to a pixel value using the Devic formula.
656
657        Args:
658        d (float): The measured dose value.
659        a (float): The a parameter of the Devic formula.
660        b (float): The b parameter of the Devic formula.
661
662        Returns:
663        float: The pixel value corresponding to the measured dose value.
664        """
665        return d / (a + b * d)
666
667    def convert_image_to_dose(self, image: np.array):
668        r"""
669        Converts an image to a dose map using the calibration curve parameters.
670
671        Args:
672        image (np.array): The input image to convert, with shape (height, width, 3).
673
674        Returns:
675        np.array: The dose map generated from the input image.
676
677        Throws:
678        ValueError: If the image does not have 3 channels.
679        """
680        if image.shape[2] != 3:
681            raise ValueError("Image must have 3 channels")
682        pv_to_dose, normed_image = self.normalize_image_by_calibration_type(image)
683        dose = np.zeros(image.shape)
684        dose[:, :, 0] = pv_to_dose(
685            normed_image[:, :, 0], *self.calibration_curve.r_opt
686        )
687        dose[:, :, 1] = pv_to_dose(
688            normed_image[:, :, 1], *self.calibration_curve.g_opt
689        )
690        dose[:, :, 2] = pv_to_dose(
691            normed_image[:, :, 2], *self.calibration_curve.b_opt
692        )
693        return dose
694
695    def save_calibration_object(self, path: str = None):
696        r"""
697        Saves the calibration object to a file using the pickle module.
698
699        Returns:
700        None
701        """
702        if not isinstance(path, str):
703            root = tk.Tk()
704            root.withdraw()
705            f = fd.asksaveasfile(
706                mode="wb",
707                defaultextension=".cal",
708                initialdir=self.calibration_file_directory,
709                title="Save calibration object",
710                confirmoverwrite=True,
711            )
712            if f is None:
713                return
714            pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
715            root.destroy()
716
717        else:
718            with open(path, "wb") as f:
719                pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
720
721    def load_calibration_object(self, path: str = None):
722        r"""
723        Opens the calibration object file and updates the current object's attributes with the loaded object's attributes.
724
725        Returns:
726        None
727        """
728        if not isinstance(path, str):
729            root = tk.Tk()
730            root.withdraw()
731            f = fd.askopenfile(
732                mode="rb",
733                parent=root,
734                initialdir="$HOME",
735                title="Select saved calibration file",
736            )
737            self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)
738            # print(calibration_object_file_path)
739            root.destroy()
740        else:
741            with open(path, "rb") as f:
742                self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)
743
744    @staticmethod
745    def create_or_load_calibration_object():
746        r"""
747        Prompts the user to create a new calibration or load an existing calibration.
748        If the user chooses to create a new calibration, a new FilmCalibration object is created,
749        configured, and saved. The calibration curve is also plotted.
750        If the user chooses to load an existing calibration, the user is prompted to select a saved
751        calibration file. The selected file is then loaded into a new FilmCalibration object, and
752        the calibration curve is plotted.
753        Raises a ValueError if the user enters an invalid input.
754        """
755        print(
756            "Please enter N to create a new calibration or L to load an existing calibration:"
757        )
758        load_or_new_calibration_str = input()
759        film_calibration = FilmCalibration()
760        if load_or_new_calibration_str == "N":
761            film_calibration.configure_calibration()
762            film_calibration.create_calibration_curve()
763            film_calibration.save_calibration_object()
764        elif load_or_new_calibration_str == "L":
765            film_calibration.load_calibration_object()
766        else:
767            raise ValueError("Invalid input. Please enter N or L.")
768        film_calibration.display_calibration_films()
769        film_calibration.calibration_curve.plot_calibration_and_response_curve()
770        return film_calibration

391        r"""
392        Loads calibration images from a dictionary of file paths and calculates the mean pixel value for each image.
393
394        Raises:
395        ValueError: If the calibration file dictionary is not set.
396
397        Returns:
398        None
399        """

401            raise ValueError("calibration file dictionary not set")
402        else:
403            self.calibration_images = {
404                j: np.mean(
405                    [tifffile.imread(i) for i in self.calibration_file_dict[j]], axis=0
406                )
407                / self.pixel_range
408                for j in self.calibration_file_dict.keys()
409            }

448    def set_roi_bounds(self, new_bounds: tuple):
449        r"""

def create_calibration_curve(self): 
466    def create_calibration_curve(self):
467        r"""
468        Create a calibration curve for a film dosimetry image.
469
470        The calibration curve is created by analyzing a set of calibration images
471        with known doses and calculating the mean pixel value in a region of
472        interest (ROI) for each color channel (red, green, blue) as a function of
473        dose. The calibration curve is then fitted to a response curve and a
474        calibration curve, which are plotted along with a dose residual plot.
475
476        Returns:
477        None
478        """
479        doses = np.array(list(self.calibration_images.keys()))
480        r_pv = np.array([])
481        g_pv = []
482        b_pv = []
483
484        r_std = []
485        g_std = []
486        b_std = []
487
488        # check that the ROI bounds are on the image, if not throw an error
489        for dose in doses:
490            print(dose, " ", self.calibration_images[dose].shape)
491            if (
492            self.roi_bounds[0] < 0
493            or self.roi_bounds[1] < 0
494            or self.roi_bounds[2] > self.calibration_images[dose].shape[1]
495            or self.roi_bounds[3] > self.calibration_images[dose].shape[0]
496            ):
497                raise ValueError(
498                    f"ROI bounds {self.roi_bounds} are outside the image with shape {self.calibration_images[dose].shape} at dose {dose}"
499                )
500
501        # populate arrays with mean pixel value in ROI as a function of dose
502        r_pv = np.array(
503            [
504                self.calibration_images[dose][
505                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
506                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
507                    0,
508                ].mean()
509                for dose in doses
510            ]
511        )
512        g_pv = np.array(
513            [
514                self.calibration_images[dose][
515                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
516                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
517                    1,
518                ].mean()
519                for dose in doses
520            ]
521        )
522        b_pv = np.array(
523            [
524                self.calibration_images[dose][
525                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
526                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
527                    2,
528                ].mean()
529                for dose in doses
530            ]
531        )
532
533        r_std = np.array(
534            [
535                self.calibration_images[dose][
536                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
537                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
538                    0,
539                ].std()
540                for dose in doses
541            ]
542        )
543        g_std = np.array(
544            [
545                self.calibration_images[dose][
546                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
547                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
548                    1,
549                ].std()
550                for dose in doses
551            ]
552        )
553        b_std = np.array(
554            [
555                self.calibration_images[dose][
556                    self.roi_bounds[1] : self.roi_bounds[3],
557                    self.roi_bounds[0] : self.roi_bounds[2],
558                    2,
559                ].std()
560                for dose in doses
561            ]
562        )
563
564        # print('red channel:', rstd)
565        # print('green channel:', gstd)
566        # print('blue channel:', bstd)
567        self.calibration_curve = CalibrationCurve(
568            doses, r_pv, g_pv, b_pv, r_std, g_std, b_std, self.calibration_curve_type
569        )

Create a calibration curve for a film dosimetry image.

The calibration curve is created by analyzing a set of calibration images with known doses and calculating the mean pixel value in a region of interest (ROI) for each color channel (red, green, blue) as a function of dose. The calibration curve is then fitted to a response curve and a calibration curve, which are plotted along with a dose residual plot.

Returns: None

def normalize_image_by_calibration_type(self, image: <built-in function array>): 
571    def normalize_image_by_calibration_type(self, image: np.array):
572        """
573        Normalizes the given image based on the calibration curve type.
574
575        Args:
576        - image: A numpy array representing the image to be normalized, with shape (height, width, 3).
577
578        Returns:
579        A tuple containing the pv_to_dose conversion function and the normalized image.
580
581        Throws:
582        ValueError: If the image does not have 3 channels.
583        """
584        if image.shape[2] != 3:
585            raise ValueError("Image must have 3 channels")
586        norm_image = np.zeros(image.shape)
587        doses = self.calibration_curve.doses
588        r_pv = self.calibration_curve.r_pv
589        g_pv = self.calibration_curve.g_pv
590        b_pv = self.calibration_curve.b_pv
591        if self.calibration_curve_type == "Lewis":
592            pv_to_dose = FilmCalibration.lewis_pv_to_dose
593            norm_image[:, :, 0] = image[:, :, 0] / r_pv[doses == 0]
594            norm_image[:, :, 1] = image[:, :, 1] / g_pv[doses == 0]
595            norm_image[:, :, 2] = image[:, :, 2] / b_pv[doses == 0]
596        elif self.calibration_curve_type == "Devic":
597            pv_to_dose = FilmCalibration.devic_pv_to_dose
598            norm_image[:, :, 0] = np.abs(image[:, :, 0] - r_pv[doses == 0])
599            norm_image[:, :, 1] = np.abs(image[:, :, 1] - g_pv[doses == 0])
600            norm_image[:, :, 2] = np.abs(image[:, :, 2] - b_pv[doses == 0])
601        else:
602            raise ValueError("Invalid calibration curve type")
603        return (pv_to_dose, norm_image)

Normalizes the given image based on the calibration curve type.

Args:

  • image: A numpy array representing the image to be normalized, with shape (height, width, 3).

Returns: A tuple containing the pv_to_dose conversion function and the normalized image.

Throws: ValueError: If the image does not have 3 channels.

@staticmethod
def lewis_dose_to_pv(d, a, b, c): 
605    @staticmethod
606    def lewis_dose_to_pv(d, a, b, c):
607        r"""
608        Calculates the PV value for a given dose using the Lewis model.
609
610        Args:
611        d (float): The dose value.
612        a (float): The a parameter of the Lewis model.
613        b (float): The b parameter of the Lewis model.
614        c (float): The c parameter of the Lewis model.
615
616        Returns:
617        float: The PV value calculated using the Lewis model.
618        """
619        return a + b / (d + c)

Calculates the PV value for a given dose using the Lewis model.

Args: d (float): The dose value. a (float): The a parameter of the Lewis model. b (float): The b parameter of the Lewis model. c (float): The c parameter of the Lewis model.

Returns: float: The PV value calculated using the Lewis model.

@staticmethod
def lewis_pv_to_dose(pv, a, b, c): 
621    @staticmethod
622    def lewis_pv_to_dose(pv, a, b, c):
623        r"""
624        Converts a given PV value to a dose value using the Lewis formula.
625
626        Args:
627        pv (float): The PV value to convert to dose.
628        a (float): The 'a' parameter of the Lewis formula.
629        b (float): The 'b' parameter of the Lewis formula.
630        c (float): The 'c' parameter of the Lewis formula.
631
632        Returns:
633        float: The dose value corresponding to the given PV value.
634        """
635        return -c + b / (pv - a)

Converts a given PV value to a dose value using the Lewis formula.

Args: pv (float): The PV value to convert to dose. a (float): The 'a' parameter of the Lewis formula. b (float): The 'b' parameter of the Lewis formula. c (float): The 'c' parameter of the Lewis formula.

Returns: float: The dose value corresponding to the given PV value.

@staticmethod
def devic_pv_to_dose(pv, a, b): 
637    @staticmethod
638    def devic_pv_to_dose(pv, a, b):
639        r"""
640        Converts a pixel value (PV) to a dose value using the Devic formula.
641
642        Args:
643        pv (float): Pixel value
644        a (float): Calibration coefficient
645        b (float): Calibration coefficient
646
647        Returns:
648        float: Dose value
649        """
650        return (a * pv) / (1 - b * pv)

Converts a pixel value (PV) to a dose value using the Devic formula.

Args: pv (float): Pixel value a (float): Calibration coefficient b (float): Calibration coefficient

Returns: float: Dose value

@staticmethod
def devic_dose_to_pv(d, a, b): 
652    @staticmethod
653    def devic_dose_to_pv(d, a, b):
654        r"""
655        Converts a measured dose value to a pixel value using the Devic formula.
656
657        Args:
658        d (float): The measured dose value.
659        a (float): The a parameter of the Devic formula.
660        b (float): The b parameter of the Devic formula.
661
662        Returns:
663        float: The pixel value corresponding to the measured dose value.
664        """
665        return d / (a + b * d)

Converts a measured dose value to a pixel value using the Devic formula.

Args: d (float): The measured dose value. a (float): The a parameter of the Devic formula. b (float): The b parameter of the Devic formula.

Returns: float: The pixel value corresponding to the measured dose value.

def convert_image_to_dose(self, image: <built-in function array>): 
667    def convert_image_to_dose(self, image: np.array):
668        r"""
669        Converts an image to a dose map using the calibration curve parameters.
670
671        Args:
672        image (np.array): The input image to convert, with shape (height, width, 3).
673
674        Returns:
675        np.array: The dose map generated from the input image.
676
677        Throws:
678        ValueError: If the image does not have 3 channels.
679        """
680        if image.shape[2] != 3:
681            raise ValueError("Image must have 3 channels")
682        pv_to_dose, normed_image = self.normalize_image_by_calibration_type(image)
683        dose = np.zeros(image.shape)
684        dose[:, :, 0] = pv_to_dose(
685            normed_image[:, :, 0], *self.calibration_curve.r_opt
686        )
687        dose[:, :, 1] = pv_to_dose(
688            normed_image[:, :, 1], *self.calibration_curve.g_opt
689        )
690        dose[:, :, 2] = pv_to_dose(
691            normed_image[:, :, 2], *self.calibration_curve.b_opt
692        )
693        return dose

Converts an image to a dose map using the calibration curve parameters.

Args: image (np.array): The input image to convert, with shape (height, width, 3).

Returns: np.array: The dose map generated from the input image.

Throws: ValueError: If the image does not have 3 channels.

695    def save_calibration_object(self, path: str = None):
696        r"""
697        Saves the calibration object to a file using the pickle module.
698
699        Returns:
700        None
701        """
702        if not isinstance(path, str):
703            root = tk.Tk()
704            root.withdraw()
705            f = fd.asksaveasfile(
706                mode="wb",
707                defaultextension=".cal",
708                initialdir=self.calibration_file_directory,
709                title="Save calibration object",
710                confirmoverwrite=True,
711            )
712            if f is None:
713                return
714            pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
715            root.destroy()
716
717        else:
718            with open(path, "wb") as f:
719                pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)

def load_calibration_object(self, path: str = None): 
721    def load_calibration_object(self, path: str = None):

@staticmethod
def create_or_load_calibration_object(): 
744    @staticmethod
745    def create_or_load_calibration_object():
746        r"""
747        Prompts the user to create a new calibration or load an existing calibration.
748        If the user chooses to create a new calibration, a new FilmCalibration object is created,
749        configured, and saved. The calibration curve is also plotted.
750        If the user chooses to load an existing calibration, the user is prompted to select a saved
751        calibration file. The selected file is then loaded into a new FilmCalibration object, and
752        the calibration curve is plotted.
753        Raises a ValueError if the user enters an invalid input.
754        """
755        print(
756            "Please enter N to create a new calibration or L to load an existing calibration:"
757        )
758        load_or_new_calibration_str = input()
759        film_calibration = FilmCalibration()
760        if load_or_new_calibration_str == "N":
761            film_calibration.configure_calibration()
762            film_calibration.create_calibration_curve()
763            film_calibration.save_calibration_object()
764        elif load_or_new_calibration_str == "L":
765            film_calibration.load_calibration_object()
766        else:
767            raise ValueError("Invalid input. Please enter N or L.")
768        film_calibration.display_calibration_films()
769        film_calibration.calibration_curve.plot_calibration_and_response_curve()
770        return film_calibration

Prompts the user to create a new calibration or load an existing calibration. If the user chooses to create a new calibration, a new FilmCalibration object is created, configured, and saved. The calibration curve is also plotted. If the user chooses to load an existing calibration, the user is prompted to select a saved calibration file. The selected file is then loaded into a new FilmCalibration object, and the calibration curve is plotted. Raises a ValueError if the user enters an invalid input.

16        r"""

31        - validate_inputs(): validates the dose setup directory.
32        """
33        self.dir_plan_export: Path = Path(dir_plan_export)
34        self.pth_dose_executable: Path = pth_dose_executable

268class RapidBrachyMC(BrachyDoseGenerator):
269    def __init__(
270        self,
271        dir_plan_export: Path | str,
272        pth_dose_executable: Path | str="http://192.168.1.11:8000/calculate_dose_mc",
273    ) -> None:
274        r"""

class RapidBrachyTG43(brachyutils.dose.BrachyDoseGenerator): 
 80class RapidBrachyTG43(BrachyDoseGenerator):
 81    def __init__(
 82        self,
 83        dir_plan_export: Union[Path, str],
 84        pth_dose_executable: Union[Path, str]="http://192.168.1.12:8000/calculate_dose_tg43",
 85    ) -> None:
 86        r"""
 87        ### Purpose:
 88        - A class to generate dose distribution using the TG43 formalism.
 89        This class uses RapidBrachyTG43 to calculate the dose distribution.
 90        """
 91        super().__init__(dir_plan_export, pth_dose_executable)
 92
 93    def generate_dose(
 94        self,
 95        dir_output: Optional[str] = None,
 96        dose_output_extension: Optional[Literal[".3ddose", ".seq.nrrd"]] = ".seq.nrrd",
 97        pth_egsphant: Optional[Path] = None,
 98        pth_plan: Optional[Path] = None,
 99        pth_mac: Optional[Path] = None,
100        num_threads: Optional[int] = 12,
101        output_dose_per_dwell: Optional[Literal[True, False, "dose_rate"]] = False,
102        dir_source_parameters: Optional[str] = "SourceParameters/microSelectron-v2",
103        using_imbt_plan: Optional[bool] = False,
104        shield_model: Optional[Literal["step", "tanh"]] = None,
105        critical_angle: Optional[float] = None,
106        correction_angle: Optional[float] = None,
107        rotation_angle_config: Optional[str] = None,
108    ):
109        r"""
110        ### Purpose:
111        - To define the input parameters for the calculate_dose function.
112
113        ### Inputs:
114        - dir_dose_setup: str := The directory where the dose setup files are stored. This directory
115            should containe the egsphant file, plan files, and mac files. it can also contain the
116            the optional applicator_geometry.json file.
117        - dir_output: Optional[str] := The directory where the dose files will be written.
118            If None, the dose files will be written to the dir_dose_setup directory.    
119        - dose_output_extension: Literal[".3ddose", ".nrrd"] := The extension of the
120            dose files that are written by the executable. The default is ".nrrd".
121        - pth_egsphant: Optional[Path] := The path to the egsphant file (.egsphant or .seq.nrrd).
122            If None, the function will search for a single .egsphant file in the dir_dose_setup directory.
123        - pth_plan: Optional[Path] := The path to the plan file (.plan).
124        - pth_mac: Optional[Path] := The path to the mac file (.mac).
125        - num_threads: Optional[int] := The number of threads to use for the calculation. The default is 4.
126        - output_dose_per_dwell: Literal[bool, str] := A flag to indicate if the dose per dwell position should be output.
127            The default is False. Other options are True and "dose_rate". for optimization, select "dose_rate".
128        - dir_source_parameters: Optional[str] := The directory where the source parameters are stored.
129            The default is "./SourceParameters/microSelectron-v2".
130        - using_imbt_plan: Optional[bool] := a binary flag to indicate if the plan is an IMBT plan.
131        - shield_model: Optional[Literal["step", "tanh"]] := The model to use for the shield. The default is None.
132        - critical_angle: Optional[float] := The critical angle for the phi dependence function, if necessary.
133        - correction_angle: Optional[float] := The correction angle for the phi dependence function, if necessary.
134        - rotation_angle_config- [optional] either a nine-character string representing the start, end, and increment
135        angles (e.g. 000220015 for IMBT delievered from 0-220 degree increments) or a path to the
136        catheter_table.json file where this information can be extracted.
137
138        ### Outputs:
139            - response: The response from the dose executable. God know what it is.
140        """
141        if output_dose_per_dwell == True:
142            output_dose_per_dwell = "true"
143        elif output_dose_per_dwell == False:
144            output_dose_per_dwell = "false"
145        elif output_dose_per_dwell == "dose_rate":
146            output_dose_per_dwell = "dose_rate"
147        else:
148            raise ValueError("Invalid value for output_dose_per_dwell.")
149
150        if pth_egsphant is None:
151            pth_egsphant = list(self.dir_plan_export.glob("*egsphant.seq.nrrd")).pop()
152        if pth_mac is None:
153            pth_mac = list(self.dir_plan_export.glob("combined.mac")).pop()
154
155        if "http" in self.pth_dose_executable:
156            # use fast api post to request the dose calculation
157            import requests
158
159            response = requests.post(
160                self.pth_dose_executable,
161                json={
162                    "dir_dose_setup": str(self.dir_plan_export),
163                    "dir_output": str(dir_output) if dir_output is not None else None,
164                    "dose_output_extension": str(dose_output_extension) if dose_output_extension is not None else None,
165                    "pth_egsphant": str(pth_egsphant) if pth_egsphant is not None else None,
166                    "pth_plan": str(pth_plan) if pth_plan is not None else None,
167                    "pth_mac": str(pth_mac) if pth_mac is not None else None,
168                    "num_threads": str(num_threads) if num_threads is not None else None,
169                    "dir_source_parameters": str(dir_source_parameters) if dir_source_parameters is not None else None,
170                    "output_dose_per_dwell": output_dose_per_dwell,
171                    "using_imbt_plan": str(using_imbt_plan) if using_imbt_plan is not None else None,
172                    "shield_model": str(shield_model) if shield_model is not None else None,
173                    "critical_angle": str(critical_angle) if critical_angle is not None else None,
174                    "correction_angle": (correction_angle) if correction_angle is not None else None,
175                    "rotation_angle_config": str(rotation_angle_config) if rotation_angle_config is not None else None,
176                },
177                timeout=None,
178            )
179            # let's handle the response here
180            if response.status_code == 200:
181                print("Dose calculation completed successfully.")
182            else:
183                raise RuntimeError(
184                    f"Dose calculation failed with status code {response.status_code}: {response.text}"
185                )
186        elif ".py" in self.pth_dose_executable:
187            # use subprocess to run the python script
188            raise NotImplementedError("This feature is not implemented yet.")
189        else:
190            raise ValueError(
191                "The dose executable is not supported. It should be a URL or a python script."
192            )
193
194        return response
195
196    def validate_inputs(self):
197        r"""
198        ### Purpose:
199        - Validate the inputs o f the TG43 dose generator.
200        """
201        assert self.dir_plan_export.exists(), "The dose setup directory does not exist."
202        # assert self.pth_dose_executable.exists(), "The dose executable does not exist."
203
204        # look through the files in dose setup directory
205        all_files: list = glob(str(self.dir_plan_export / "*"))
206        assert len(all_files) > 0, "The dose setup directory is empty."
207        assert any(".plan" in file for file in all_files), "The plan file is missing."
208        assert any(
209            ".egsphant" in file for file in all_files
210        ), "The egsphant file is missing."
211        assert any(".mac" in file for file in all_files), "The mac file is missing."
212
213    def run_dose_generation(
214        self,
215        plan: BrachyPlan,
216        generate_dose_rate_maps: bool = False,
217        export_config_brachyplan: ExportConfig_BrachyPlan | bool | dict = None,
218        ) -> BrachyPlan:
219        r"""
220        ### Purpose:
221        - to run the dose generation for the plan and return a plan with combined dose filled as well
222        as the dose rate dictionary if desired.
223
224        ### Inputs:
225        - plan:= The treatment plan for which we want to generate the dose. 
226        - generate_dose_rate_maps := whether to generate dose rate maps for each dwell position.
227        If True, the dose_rate_dict will be populated with the dose rate maps for each dwell position.
228        - export_config_brachyplan := If false, we assume the egsphant, mac files, and plan files have been
229        exported before. If True or None, we create a default ExportConfig_BrachyPlan to export the setup files
230        needed for RapidBrachyTG43. You can also provide your own custom export config.
231
232        ### Output:
233        - plan: BrachyPlan := The brachy plan with the combined dose and optionally the dose rate dict filled.
234        """
235        if export_config_brachyplan is None or export_config_brachyplan == True:
236            export_config_brachyplan = ExportConfig_BrachyPlan(
237                dir_export=self.dir_plan_export,
238                export_config_egsphant=True,
239                export_config_plan_and_mac=True,
240            )
241        elif isinstance(export_config_brachyplan, dict):
242            export_config_brachyplan = ExportConfig_BrachyPlan(**export_config_brachyplan)
243
244        if export_config_brachyplan:
245            plan.export_brachy_plan(export_config_brachyplan)
246
247        # call the dose generator to generate the dose maps
248        self.generate_dose(
249            pth_mac=export_config_brachyplan.export_config_plan_and_mac.pth_mac_combined,
250            pth_plan=export_config_brachyplan.export_config_plan_and_mac.pth_plan_combined,
251            output_dose_per_dwell= "dose_rate" if generate_dose_rate_maps else False,
252        )
253
254        pth_combined_dose = export_config_brachyplan.export_config_plan_and_mac.pth_mac_combined.with_suffix(".seq.nrrd")
255
256        # load the generated dose maps and update the plan
257        if generate_dose_rate_maps:
258            plan.catheter_table.load_dose_rates(
259                dir_dose_rate=self.dir_plan_export,
260            )
261        else:
262            # Export the combined dose file, overwriting the tg43 automatically generated file 
263            combined_dose = BrachyDose(pth_combined_dose)
264            combined_dose.write_to_nrrd(pth_combined_dose)
265            plan.catheter_table.set_combined_dose(combined_dose)
266        return plan

172                    "shield_model": str(shield_model) if shield_model is not None else None,
173                    "critical_angle": str(critical_angle) if critical_angle is not None else None,
174                    "correction_angle": (correction_angle) if correction_angle is not None else None,
175                    "rotation_angle_config": str(rotation_angle_config) if rotation_angle_config is not None else None,
176                },
177                timeout=None,
178            )
179            # let's handle the response here
180            if response.status_code == 200:
181                print("Dose calculation completed successfully.")
182            else:
183                raise RuntimeError(
184                    f"Dose calculation failed with status code {response.status_code}: {response.text}"
185                )
186        elif ".py" in self.pth_dose_executable:
187            # use subprocess to run the python script
188            raise NotImplementedError("This feature is not implemented yet.")
189        else:
190            raise ValueError(
191                "The dose executable is not supported. It should be a URL or a python script."
192            )
193
194        return response

Purpose:

  • To define the input parameters for the calculate_dose function.

Inputs:

  • dir_dose_setup: str := The directory where the dose setup files are stored. This directory should containe the egsphant file, plan files, and mac files. it can also contain the the optional applicator_geometry.json file.
  • dir_output: Optional[str] := The directory where the dose files will be written. If None, the dose files will be written to the dir_dose_setup directory.
  • dose_output_extension: Literal[".3ddose", ".nrrd"] := The extension of the dose files that are written by the executable. The default is ".nrrd".
  • pth_egsphant: Optional[Path] := The path to the egsphant file (.egsphant or .seq.nrrd). If None, the function will search for a single .egsphant file in the dir_dose_setup directory.
  • pth_plan: Optional[Path] := The path to the plan file (.plan).
  • pth_mac: Optional[Path] := The path to the mac file (.mac).
  • num_threads: Optional[int] := The number of threads to use for the calculation. The default is 4.
  • output_dose_per_dwell: Literal[bool, str] := A flag to indicate if the dose per dwell position should be output. The default is False. Other options are True and "dose_rate". for optimization, select "dose_rate".
  • dir_source_parameters: Optional[str] := The directory where the source parameters are stored. The default is "./SourceParameters/microSelectron-v2".
  • using_imbt_plan: Optional[bool] := a binary flag to indicate if the plan is an IMBT plan.
  • shield_model: Optional[Literal["step", "tanh"]] := The model to use for the shield. The default is None.
  • critical_angle: Optional[float] := The critical angle for the phi dependence function, if necessary.
  • correction_angle: Optional[float] := The correction angle for the phi dependence function, if necessary.
  • rotation_angle_config- [optional] either a nine-character string representing the start, end, and increment angles (e.g. 000220015 for IMBT delievered from 0-220 degree increments) or a path to the catheter_table.json file where this information can be extracted.

Outputs:

- response: The response from the dose executable. God know what it is.

def run_dose_generation( self, plan: brachyutils.planning.BrachyPlan, generate_dose_rate_maps: bool = False, export_config_brachyplan: brachyutils.planning.plan_export_configs.ExportConfig_BrachyPlan | bool | dict = None) -> brachyutils.planning.BrachyPlan: 
213    def run_dose_generation(
214        self,
215        plan: BrachyPlan,
216        generate_dose_rate_maps: bool = False,
217        export_config_brachyplan: ExportConfig_BrachyPlan | bool | dict = None,
218        ) -> BrachyPlan:
219        r"""
220        ### Purpose:
221        - to run the dose generation for the plan and return a plan with combined dose filled as well
222        as the dose rate dictionary if desired.
223
224        ### Inputs:
225        - plan:= The treatment plan for which we want to generate the dose. 
226        - generate_dose_rate_maps := whether to generate dose rate maps for each dwell position.
227        If True, the dose_rate_dict will be populated with the dose rate maps for each dwell position.
228        - export_config_brachyplan := If false, we assume the egsphant, mac files, and plan files have been
229        exported before. If True or None, we create a default ExportConfig_BrachyPlan to export the setup files
230        needed for RapidBrachyTG43. You can also provide your own custom export config.
231
232        ### Output:
233        - plan: BrachyPlan := The brachy plan with the combined dose and optionally the dose rate dict filled.
234        """
235        if export_config_brachyplan is None or export_config_brachyplan == True:
236            export_config_brachyplan = ExportConfig_BrachyPlan(
237                dir_export=self.dir_plan_export,
238                export_config_egsphant=True,
239                export_config_plan_and_mac=True,
240            )
241        elif isinstance(export_config_brachyplan, dict):
242            export_config_brachyplan = ExportConfig_BrachyPlan(**export_config_brachyplan)
243
244        if export_config_brachyplan:
245            plan.export_brachy_plan(export_config_brachyplan)
246
247        # call the dose generator to generate the dose maps
248        self.generate_dose(
249            pth_mac=export_config_brachyplan.export_config_plan_and_mac.pth_mac_combined,
250            pth_plan=export_config_brachyplan.export_config_plan_and_mac.pth_plan_combined,
251            output_dose_per_dwell= "dose_rate" if generate_dose_rate_maps else False,
252        )
253
254        pth_combined_dose = export_config_brachyplan.export_config_plan_and_mac.pth_mac_combined.with_suffix(".seq.nrrd")
255
256        # load the generated dose maps and update the plan
257        if generate_dose_rate_maps:
258            plan.catheter_table.load_dose_rates(
259                dir_dose_rate=self.dir_plan_export,
260            )
261        else:
262            # Export the combined dose file, overwriting the tg43 automatically generated file 
263            combined_dose = BrachyDose(pth_combined_dose)
264            combined_dose.write_to_nrrd(pth_combined_dose)
265            plan.catheter_table.set_combined_dose(combined_dose)
266        return plan

def convert_dose_files( pth_inputs: List[Union[pathlib._local.Path, str]], type_out: Literal['.nrrd', '.dcm', '.3ddose'] = '.nrrd', dir_output: Union[pathlib._local.Path, str, NoneType] = None, multi_proc: bool = False) -> None: 
1383def convert_dose_files(
1384    pth_inputs: List[Union[Path, str]],
1385    type_out: Literal[".nrrd", ".dcm", ".3ddose"] = ".nrrd",
1386    dir_output: Optional[Union[Path, str]] = None,
1387    multi_proc: bool = False
1388) -> None:
1389    """
1390    Convert dose files to the specified output format.
1391    
1392    Args:
1393        pth_inputs: List of paths to input dose files. Can be directories or files.
1394        type_out: Output file type. Options are ".nrrd", ".dcm", ".3ddose".
1395        dir_output: Output directory path (optional).
1396        multi_proc: Whether to use multiprocessing (default: False).
1397    """
1398    # Main conversion logic
1399    data_to_load = []
1400    
1401    # Process each input path
1402    for pth_input in pth_inputs:
1403        pth_input = Path(pth_input)
1404        if not pth_input.exists():
1405            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Input file {pth_input} does not exist.")
1406        
1407        # Handle directories (DICOM)
1408        if pth_input.is_dir():
1409            dicom_data = _handle_dicom_directory_dose(pth_input)
1410            data_to_load.extend(dicom_data)
1411        
1412        # Handle single files
1413        elif pth_input.is_file():
1414            data_to_load.append(_prepare_dose_loading_item(pth_input))
1415        else:
1416            raise ValueError(f"Input {pth_input} is neither a file nor a directory.")
1417    
1418    # Check if we have valid items to process
1419    if not data_to_load:
1420        raise ValueError("No valid dose files found to convert.")
1421    
1422    # Setup output directory
1423    if dir_output is None:
1424        dir_output = Path(pth_inputs[0]).parent
1425    else:
1426        dir_output = Path(dir_output)
1427    dir_output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1428    
1429    # Perform conversion
1430    if multi_proc:
1431        # Create partial function with fixed arguments
1432        partial_conversion = partial(_perform_dose_conversion, dir_output=dir_output, type_out=type_out)
1433        with Pool() as pool:
1434            list(tqdm(pool.imap(partial_conversion, data_to_load), total=len(data_to_load), desc="Converting dose files"))
1435    else:
1436        for item in tqdm(data_to_load):
1437            _perform_dose_conversion(item, dir_output, type_out)

class BrachyUtilsTG43(brachyutils.dose.BrachyDoseGenerator): 
 33class BrachyUtilsTG43(BrachyDoseGenerator):
 34    """
 35    """
 36    def __init__(self,
 37        dir_tg43_parameters: Optional[str] = "SourceParameters/microSelectron-v2",
 38        dir_output : Optional[Union[Path, str]] = Path(),
 39        **calc_parameter_kwargs
 40        ) -> None:
 41        """
 42        """
 43        #input
 44        super().__init__(dir_output, None)
 45        self.dir_tg43_parameters : Path = dir_tg43_parameters
 46
 47        #store meta-parameters about the calculation in this dictionary
 48        self.calc_parameters = {
 49            "kernel_half_width" : 20 * CM, #half width to calculate dose rate kernel
 50            "kernel_res" : 0.1 * CM, #resolution to calculate the dose rate kernel
 51            "kernel_max_dose_rate": 10, #Gy/s
 52            "epsilon": 1e-3 #just a little nudge to certain values :)
 53        }
 54        self.calc_parameters.update(calc_parameter_kwargs)
 55
 56        #populate attributes to the validated brachyplan input
 57        self.brachyplan = None
 58        self.brachyphantom : BrachyPhantom = None
 59        self.brachysource : BrachySource = None#
 60        self.source_name : str = None#self.brachysource.source_geometry
 61        self.is_hdr : bool = True#self.brachysource.treatment_type == "HDR"
 62
 63        #tg43 parameters
 64        self.active_length : float = None
 65        self.air_kerma_strength : float = None
 66        self.activity : float = None
 67        self.dose_rate_constant : float = None
 68        self.radial_dose_function: Callable[[float], float] = None #TODO: fix function signatures
 69        self.geometry_function: Callable[[float, float], float] = None
 70        self.anisotropy_function : Callable[[float, float], float] = None
 71
 72        self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel : BrachyDose = None #dose rate distribution in 3D with centered source

 75
 76    def validate_brachyplan(self, plan : BrachyPlan) -> None:
 77        if plan is None:
 78            raise ValueError("Input BrachyPlan is None.")
 79        if plan.phantom is None:
 80            raise ValueError("Input BrachyPhantom has no BrachyPhantom.")
 81        if plan.simulation_setup is None:
 82            raise ValueError("Input BrachyPlan has no BrachySimulation.")
 83        if plan.simulation_setup.brachy_source is None:
 84            raise ValueError("Input BrachyPlan's BrachySimulation has no BrachySource.")
 85
 86    
 87    def load_from_brachyplan(self, plan : BrachyPlan) -> None:
 88        self.validate_brachyplan(plan)
 89        self.brachyplan = plan
 90        self.brachyphantom : BrachyPhantom = plan.phantom
 91        self.brachysource : BrachySource = plan.simulation_setup.brachy_source
 92        self.source_name : str = self.brachysource.source_geometry
 93        self.is_hdr : bool = self.brachysource.treatment_type == "HDR"
 94        #a little hard-coded fix :)
 95        if self.source_name == "MicroSelectronV2":
 96            self.source_name = "microSelectron-v2"
 97        self.air_kerma_strength = self.brachysource.reference_air_kerma_rate * U
 98        self.activity = self.brachysource.activity #can specify the (total) activity in place of the AKS
 99        if self.activity is not None:
100            self.activity *= CI
101
102    def load_and_initialize_tg43(self) -> None:
103        #Load and initialize all of the TG-43 parameters and functions
104        #NOTE: all distance dimensions should be converted 
105        logging.info("Loading TG-43 parameters.")
106        self.load_and_initialize_source_info()
107        self.load_and_initialze_aks_drc()
108        self.initialize_geometry_function()
109        self.load_and_initialize_radial_dose_function()
110        self.load_and_initialize_anisotropy_function()
111        logging.info("TG-43 parameters initialized. Computing dose-rate kernel.")
112        if logging.root.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):

114        else:
115            self.compute_tg43_dose_rate_kernel()
116        logging.info("TG-43 dose-rate kernel initialized.")

118    def load_and_initialize_source_info(self) -> None:
119        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / "source.csv"
120        with open(file_path, encoding='utf-8') as file:
121            file_data = file.readlines()[0].split(',')
122        file_data[2] = file_data[2][:-1] #cut out newline
123        if file_data[0] != self.source_name:
124            raise ValueError(f"Potential mismatch! Loaded parameters for source {file_data[0, 0]} \
125but source name is {self.source_name}.")
126        source_core_from_plan = self.brachysource.core_material.split('_')[1] + "-" + str(self.brachysource.mass_number)
127        if file_data[2] != source_core_from_plan:
128            raise ValueError(f"Potential mismatch! Loaded parameters for source isotope ###{file_data[2]}### \
129                but source core is ###{source_core_from_plan}###.")
130        self.active_length = float(file_data[1]) * CM
131        logging.debug("Active length %s mm", self.active_length)
132
133    def load_and_initialze_aks_drc(self) -> None:
134        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / f"{self.source_name}_AKS_DRC.csv"
135        file_data = np.loadtxt(file_path, dtype=np.float32, delimiter = ',', skiprows=1, usecols = [1, 2])
136        if self.air_kerma_strength is None:
137            self.air_kerma_strength = self.activity * file_data[0, 0] * U
138            logging.info("Updated air-kerma strength to %s from activity.", self.air_kerma_strength)
139        self.dose_rate_constant = file_data[0, 1] / (CM * CM)
140        logging.debug("AKS: %s Gy mm^2 s^-1; DRC: %s mm^-2", self.air_kerma_strength, self.dose_rate_constant)
141
142    def initialize_geometry_function(self) -> None:
143        def geometry_function(r_theta : np.ndarray) -> np.array:
144            r = r_theta[:,0]
145            theta = r_theta[:, 1]
146            branch_1 = np.logical_and(theta > 0.0, theta < 180.0)
147            r_branch_1 = r[branch_1]
148            r_branch_2 = r[np.logical_not(branch_1)]
149            theta_branch_1 = theta[branch_1]
150            theta_branch_1_rad = np.deg2rad(theta_branch_1)
151            ell_over_two = 0.5 * self.active_length
152
153            G = np.zeros(r_theta.shape[0])
154
155            #branch 1 - 0 < theta < 180
156            top11 = r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad) - ell_over_two
157            top12 = np.sqrt(r_branch_1 * r_branch_1 + ell_over_two * ell_over_two - (self.active_length * r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad)))
158            top21 = r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad) + ell_over_two
159            top22 = np.sqrt(r_branch_1 * r_branch_1  + ell_over_two*ell_over_two + self.active_length * r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad))
160            bottom = self.active_length * r_branch_1 * np.sin(theta_branch_1_rad)
161            #top1 = np.clip(top11/top12, a_min = -1.0, a_max = 1.0) #some rounding errors causing issues with acos
162            #top2 = np.clip(top21/top22, a_min = -1.0, a_max = 1.0)
163            top = np.arccos(top11/top12)-np.arccos(top21/top22)
164            G[branch_1] = (top/bottom)#[branch_1]
165
166            #branch 2 - theta = 0 or theta = 180
167            G[~branch_1] = 1.0 / (r_branch_2 * r_branch_2 - ell_over_two * ell_over_two)
168
169            return G
170        self.geometry_function = geometry_function
171
172    def load_and_initialize_radial_dose_function(self) -> None:
173        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / f"{self.source_name}_radialdosefunction.csv"
174        file_data = np.loadtxt(file_path, delimiter=',', skiprows=1, dtype = np.float16)
175        radii = file_data[:,0] * CM
176        radii_meshgrid = np.meshgrid(radii)
177        
178        radial_dose_function_data = file_data[:,1]
179        #print(radii_mm.shape, radial_dose_function_data.shape)
180        if self.is_hdr:
181            radial_dose_function_interpolator = RegularGridInterpolator(radii_meshgrid, radial_dose_function_data, method='linear', bounds_error=False)
182            def radial_dose_function(r: np.array) -> np.array:
183                gr = radial_dose_function_interpolator(r)
184                if np.all(~np.isnan(gr)):
185                    return gr
186                gr[r < radii[0]] = radial_dose_function_data[0] #r<rmin nearest neighbor extrapolation
187                gr[r > radii[-1]] = \
188                radial_dose_function_data[-2] + \
189                ((radial_dose_function_data[-1] -radial_dose_function_data[-2]) / (radii[-1] - radii[-2])) \
190                * (r[r > radii[-1]] - radii[-2]) #r>rmax linear extrapolation
191                return gr
192        else:
193            raise NotImplementedError("TG-43 for LDR not yet implemented.")
194        self.radial_dose_function = radial_dose_function
195
196    def load_and_initialize_anisotropy_function(self) -> None:
197        #load the data
198        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / f"{self.source_name}_2danisotropyfunction.csv"
199        file_data = np.genfromtxt(file_path,dtype=str, delimiter=',')
200        file_data_F = file_data[:file_data.shape[0] // 2, :] #exclude the uncertainty
201        file_data_F[file_data_F == '-'] = "-1" #points inside the source
202        radii = np.array(file_data_F[1:, 0], dtype=np.float16) * CM
203        thetas = np.array(file_data_F[0, 1:], dtype = np.float16)
204        anisotropy_function_data = np.array(file_data_F[1:, 1:], dtype = np.float16)
205
206        #nearest neigbor extrapolate the points of the anisotropy function in the source
207        for ir in range(radii.size):
208            Fr = anisotropy_function_data[ir, :]
209            if(np.all(Fr > 0)):
210                continue
211            ithetamin = np.min(np.where(Fr > 0))
212            ithetamax = np.max(np.where(Fr > 0))
213            thetamin = thetas[ithetamin]
214            thetamax = thetas[ithetamax]
215            Fr[thetas < thetamin] = Fr[ithetamin]
216            Fr[thetas > thetamax] = Fr[ithetamax]
217            anisotropy_function_data[ir] = Fr
218
219        anisotropy_function_interpolator = RegularGridInterpolator((radii, thetas), anisotropy_function_data, method='linear', bounds_error=False)
220        def anisotropy_function(r_theta : np.ndarray) -> np.array: #N x 2 array -> N array
221            F = anisotropy_function_interpolator(r_theta)
222            for ir_in in np.where(np.isnan(F))[0]:
223                itheta = np.argmin(np.abs(r_theta[ir_in,1] - thetas))
224                r_in = r_theta[ir_in, 0]
225                if r_in < radii[0]:
226                    ir = 0
227                else:
228                    ir = -1
229                F[ir_in] = anisotropy_function_data[ir, itheta]
230            return F
231        self.anisotropy_function = anisotropy_function
232
233    def compute_tg43_dose_rate_kernel(self, debug_pth_out : Path = None) -> None:
234
235        kernel_half_width = self.calc_parameters["kernel_half_width"]
236        kernel_res = self.calc_parameters["kernel_res"]
237        epsilon = self.calc_parameters["epsilon"]
238        kernel_axis = np.arange(-kernel_half_width, kernel_half_width + epsilon, kernel_res, dtype = np.float32)
239        kernel_axis_size = kernel_axis.size
240        kernel_shape = (kernel_axis_size, kernel_axis_size, kernel_axis_size)
241        kernel_x, kernel_y, kernel_z = np.meshgrid(kernel_axis, kernel_axis, kernel_axis)
242        kernel_r = np.sqrt(kernel_x * kernel_x + kernel_y * kernel_y + kernel_z * kernel_z)
243        kernel_r[np.isclose(kernel_r, 0., epsilon)] = epsilon
244        #theta is off the z_axis (0, 0, 1), angle between two vectors a,b is arccos(a*b/(|a||b|))
245        #this means that theta is just arccos(z/r)
246        kernel_theta = np.arccos(kernel_z / kernel_r) * RAD
247    
248        del kernel_x
249        del kernel_y
250        del kernel_z
251
252        logging.debug("Initializing AKS * DRC grid.")
253        kernel_array = self.air_kerma_strength * self.dose_rate_constant / self.geometry_function(np.array([[10., 90.0]])) * np.ones(kernel_shape, dtype = np.float16)
254
255        kernel_r_theta = np.column_stack((kernel_r.flatten(), kernel_theta.flatten()))
256        #del kernel_r
257        #del kernel_theta
258        logging.debug("AKS * DRC grid initialized.")
259        #geometry fn
260        logging.debug("Initializing geometry function grid.")
261        kernel_geometry_function = np.reshape(self.geometry_function(kernel_r_theta), kernel_shape)
262        if np.any(kernel_geometry_function == 0):
263            where_zero = kernel_geometry_function == 0
264            raise UserWarning(f"Kernel's geometry function has 0s at r={kernel_r[where_zero]}/theta={kernel_theta[where_zero]}.")
265        kernel_array *= kernel_geometry_function
266        del kernel_geometry_function
267
268        logging.debug("Geometry function grid initialized.")
269        #radial dose fn
270        logging.debug("Initializing radial dose function grid.")
271        kernel_radial_dose_function = np.reshape(self.radial_dose_function(kernel_r_theta[:,0]), kernel_shape)
272        kernel_array *= kernel_radial_dose_function
273        del kernel_radial_dose_function
274        logging.debug("Radial dose functiong grid initialized.")
275
276        #anistropy fn
277        logging.debug("Initializing 2D anisotropy function grid.")
278        kernel_anisotropy_function = np.reshape(self.anisotropy_function(kernel_r_theta), kernel_shape)
279        kernel_array *= kernel_anisotropy_function
280        logging.debug("2D anisotropy function grid initialized.")
281        if np.any(kernel_anisotropy_function == 0):
282            where_zero = kernel_anisotropy_function == 0
283            raise UserWarning(f"Kernel's anisotropy function has 0s at r={kernel_r[where_zero]}/theta={kernel_theta[where_zero]}.")
284        del kernel_anisotropy_function
285        #make the dose image
286        if np.any(np.isnan(kernel_array)):
287            print(kernel_r[np.where(np.isnan(kernel_array))], kernel_theta[np.where(np.isnan(kernel_array))])
288            raise ValueError("NaN dose rate values in the TG-43 dose rate kernel.")
289
290        np.clip(kernel_array, a_min = 0.0, a_max = self.calc_parameters["kernel_max_dose_rate"], out=kernel_array)
291        logging.debug("Generating TG-43 dose rate kernel image.")
292        kernel_dose_image = DoseImage(imageArray=kernel_array, name='TG-43 Dose Kernel',
293            origin=(-kernel_half_width,-kernel_half_width,-kernel_half_width), spacing = (kernel_res, kernel_res, kernel_res))
294        self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel = BrachyDose(dtype=np.float16)
295        self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel.dose_image = kernel_dose_image
296        if debug_pth_out is not None:
297            logging.debug("Writing dose rate kernel to path %s", debug_pth_out)
298            self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel.write_brachydose_to_file(debug_pth_out)
299        logging.debug("TG-43 dose rate kernel generation complete.")

302        #check that the brachyplan has the required info before proceeding

305        #and a BrachySimulatinos

313    def run_dose_generation(
314        self,
315        dir_export: str | Path = None,
316        plan: BrachyPlan = None,
317        generate_dose_rate_maps: bool = True,
318        export_combined_dose:bool = False) -> BrachyPlan:
319        if not generate_dose_rate_maps:
320            raise ValueError("generate_dose_rate_maps must be True in BrachyUtilsTG43.")
321
322        self.load_from_brachyplan(plan)
323        self.load_and_initialize_tg43()
324        self.validate_inputs()
325
326        #with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
327        with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
328            futures = {executor.submit(calculate_dwell_dose_tg43, dwell, self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel, self.brachyphantom): dwell for dwell in self.brachyplan.catheter_table.all_dwells}
329            for action in tqdm(
330                as_completed(futures),
331                total = len( self.brachyplan.catheter_table.all_dwells),
332                desc = "Calculating dwell doses:"):
333                    try:
334                        action.result()
335                    except Exception as exc:
336                        failed_dwell = futures[action]
337                        raise ValueError(f"TG-43DoseCalculator failed for dwell {failed_dwell.name_id}") from exc
338
339        logging.info("TG-43 dose calculation complete.")
340        if export_combined_dose:
341            combined_dose = self.brachyplan.combined_dose
342            if dir_export is None:
343                dir_export = Path(self.dir_plan_export)
344            else:
345                dir_export = Path(dir_export)
346            pth_output = dir_export / "combined_TG43.seq.nrrd"
347            logging.info("Writing combined TG-43 dose to %s.", pth_output)
348            combined_dose.write_brachydose_to_file(pth_output)
349

351        raise NotImplementedError("generate_dose() not implemented for BrachyUtilsTG43. Call run_dose_generation() instead.")

118    def load_and_initialize_source_info(self) -> None:
119        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / "source.csv"
120        with open(file_path, encoding='utf-8') as file:
121            file_data = file.readlines()[0].split(',')
122        file_data[2] = file_data[2][:-1] #cut out newline

127        if file_data[2] != source_core_from_plan:

130        self.active_length = float(file_data[1]) * CM
131        logging.debug("Active length %s mm", self.active_length)
def load_and_initialze_aks_drc(self) -> None: 
133    def load_and_initialze_aks_drc(self) -> None:
134        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / f"{self.source_name}_AKS_DRC.csv"
135        file_data = np.loadtxt(file_path, dtype=np.float32, delimiter = ',', skiprows=1, usecols = [1, 2])
136        if self.air_kerma_strength is None:
137            self.air_kerma_strength = self.activity * file_data[0, 0] * U
138            logging.info("Updated air-kerma strength to %s from activity.", self.air_kerma_strength)
139        self.dose_rate_constant = file_data[0, 1] / (CM * CM)

def initialize_geometry_function(self) -> None: 
142    def initialize_geometry_function(self) -> None:
143        def geometry_function(r_theta : np.ndarray) -> np.array:
144            r = r_theta[:,0]
145            theta = r_theta[:, 1]
146            branch_1 = np.logical_and(theta > 0.0, theta < 180.0)
147            r_branch_1 = r[branch_1]
148            r_branch_2 = r[np.logical_not(branch_1)]
149            theta_branch_1 = theta[branch_1]
150            theta_branch_1_rad = np.deg2rad(theta_branch_1)
151            ell_over_two = 0.5 * self.active_length
152
153            G = np.zeros(r_theta.shape[0])
154
155            #branch 1 - 0 < theta < 180
156            top11 = r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad) - ell_over_two
157            top12 = np.sqrt(r_branch_1 * r_branch_1 + ell_over_two * ell_over_two - (self.active_length * r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad)))
158            top21 = r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad) + ell_over_two
159            top22 = np.sqrt(r_branch_1 * r_branch_1  + ell_over_two*ell_over_two + self.active_length * r_branch_1 * np.cos(theta_branch_1_rad))
160            bottom = self.active_length * r_branch_1 * np.sin(theta_branch_1_rad)
161            #top1 = np.clip(top11/top12, a_min = -1.0, a_max = 1.0) #some rounding errors causing issues with acos
162            #top2 = np.clip(top21/top22, a_min = -1.0, a_max = 1.0)
163            top = np.arccos(top11/top12)-np.arccos(top21/top22)
164            G[branch_1] = (top/bottom)#[branch_1]
165
166            #branch 2 - theta = 0 or theta = 180
167            G[~branch_1] = 1.0 / (r_branch_2 * r_branch_2 - ell_over_two * ell_over_two)
168
169            return G
170        self.geometry_function = geometry_function
def load_and_initialize_radial_dose_function(self) -> None: 
172    def load_and_initialize_radial_dose_function(self) -> None:
173        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / f"{self.source_name}_radialdosefunction.csv"
174        file_data = np.loadtxt(file_path, delimiter=',', skiprows=1, dtype = np.float16)
175        radii = file_data[:,0] * CM
176        radii_meshgrid = np.meshgrid(radii)
177        
178        radial_dose_function_data = file_data[:,1]
179        #print(radii_mm.shape, radial_dose_function_data.shape)
180        if self.is_hdr:
181            radial_dose_function_interpolator = RegularGridInterpolator(radii_meshgrid, radial_dose_function_data, method='linear', bounds_error=False)
182            def radial_dose_function(r: np.array) -> np.array:
183                gr = radial_dose_function_interpolator(r)
184                if np.all(~np.isnan(gr)):
185                    return gr
186                gr[r < radii[0]] = radial_dose_function_data[0] #r<rmin nearest neighbor extrapolation
187                gr[r > radii[-1]] = \
188                radial_dose_function_data[-2] + \
189                ((radial_dose_function_data[-1] -radial_dose_function_data[-2]) / (radii[-1] - radii[-2])) \
190                * (r[r > radii[-1]] - radii[-2]) #r>rmax linear extrapolation
191                return gr
192        else:
193            raise NotImplementedError("TG-43 for LDR not yet implemented.")
194        self.radial_dose_function = radial_dose_function
def load_and_initialize_anisotropy_function(self) -> None: 
196    def load_and_initialize_anisotropy_function(self) -> None:
197        #load the data
198        file_path = self.dir_tg43_parameters / f"{self.source_name}_2danisotropyfunction.csv"
199        file_data = np.genfromtxt(file_path,dtype=str, delimiter=',')
200        file_data_F = file_data[:file_data.shape[0] // 2, :] #exclude the uncertainty
201        file_data_F[file_data_F == '-'] = "-1" #points inside the source
202        radii = np.array(file_data_F[1:, 0], dtype=np.float16) * CM
203        thetas = np.array(file_data_F[0, 1:], dtype = np.float16)
204        anisotropy_function_data = np.array(file_data_F[1:, 1:], dtype = np.float16)
205
206        #nearest neigbor extrapolate the points of the anisotropy function in the source
207        for ir in range(radii.size):
208            Fr = anisotropy_function_data[ir, :]
209            if(np.all(Fr > 0)):
210                continue
211            ithetamin = np.min(np.where(Fr > 0))
212            ithetamax = np.max(np.where(Fr > 0))
213            thetamin = thetas[ithetamin]
214            thetamax = thetas[ithetamax]
215            Fr[thetas < thetamin] = Fr[ithetamin]
216            Fr[thetas > thetamax] = Fr[ithetamax]
217            anisotropy_function_data[ir] = Fr
218
219        anisotropy_function_interpolator = RegularGridInterpolator((radii, thetas), anisotropy_function_data, method='linear', bounds_error=False)
220        def anisotropy_function(r_theta : np.ndarray) -> np.array: #N x 2 array -> N array
221            F = anisotropy_function_interpolator(r_theta)
222            for ir_in in np.where(np.isnan(F))[0]:
223                itheta = np.argmin(np.abs(r_theta[ir_in,1] - thetas))
224                r_in = r_theta[ir_in, 0]
225                if r_in < radii[0]:
226                    ir = 0
227                else:
228                    ir = -1
229                F[ir_in] = anisotropy_function_data[ir, itheta]
230            return F
231        self.anisotropy_function = anisotropy_function
def compute_tg43_dose_rate_kernel(self, debug_pth_out: pathlib._local.Path = None) -> None: 
233    def compute_tg43_dose_rate_kernel(self, debug_pth_out : Path = None) -> None:
234
235        kernel_half_width = self.calc_parameters["kernel_half_width"]
236        kernel_res = self.calc_parameters["kernel_res"]
237        epsilon = self.calc_parameters["epsilon"]
238        kernel_axis = np.arange(-kernel_half_width, kernel_half_width + epsilon, kernel_res, dtype = np.float32)
239        kernel_axis_size = kernel_axis.size
240        kernel_shape = (kernel_axis_size, kernel_axis_size, kernel_axis_size)
241        kernel_x, kernel_y, kernel_z = np.meshgrid(kernel_axis, kernel_axis, kernel_axis)
242        kernel_r = np.sqrt(kernel_x * kernel_x + kernel_y * kernel_y + kernel_z * kernel_z)
243        kernel_r[np.isclose(kernel_r, 0., epsilon)] = epsilon
244        #theta is off the z_axis (0, 0, 1), angle between two vectors a,b is arccos(a*b/(|a||b|))
245        #this means that theta is just arccos(z/r)
246        kernel_theta = np.arccos(kernel_z / kernel_r) * RAD
247    
248        del kernel_x
249        del kernel_y
250        del kernel_z
251
252        logging.debug("Initializing AKS * DRC grid.")
253        kernel_array = self.air_kerma_strength * self.dose_rate_constant / self.geometry_function(np.array([[10., 90.0]])) * np.ones(kernel_shape, dtype = np.float16)
254
255        kernel_r_theta = np.column_stack((kernel_r.flatten(), kernel_theta.flatten()))
256        #del kernel_r
257        #del kernel_theta
258        logging.debug("AKS * DRC grid initialized.")
259        #geometry fn
260        logging.debug("Initializing geometry function grid.")
261        kernel_geometry_function = np.reshape(self.geometry_function(kernel_r_theta), kernel_shape)
262        if np.any(kernel_geometry_function == 0):
263            where_zero = kernel_geometry_function == 0
264            raise UserWarning(f"Kernel's geometry function has 0s at r={kernel_r[where_zero]}/theta={kernel_theta[where_zero]}.")
265        kernel_array *= kernel_geometry_function
266        del kernel_geometry_function
267
268        logging.debug("Geometry function grid initialized.")
269        #radial dose fn
270        logging.debug("Initializing radial dose function grid.")
271        kernel_radial_dose_function = np.reshape(self.radial_dose_function(kernel_r_theta[:,0]), kernel_shape)
272        kernel_array *= kernel_radial_dose_function
273        del kernel_radial_dose_function
274        logging.debug("Radial dose functiong grid initialized.")
275
276        #anistropy fn
277        logging.debug("Initializing 2D anisotropy function grid.")
278        kernel_anisotropy_function = np.reshape(self.anisotropy_function(kernel_r_theta), kernel_shape)
279        kernel_array *= kernel_anisotropy_function
280        logging.debug("2D anisotropy function grid initialized.")
281        if np.any(kernel_anisotropy_function == 0):
282            where_zero = kernel_anisotropy_function == 0
283            raise UserWarning(f"Kernel's anisotropy function has 0s at r={kernel_r[where_zero]}/theta={kernel_theta[where_zero]}.")
284        del kernel_anisotropy_function
285        #make the dose image
286        if np.any(np.isnan(kernel_array)):
287            print(kernel_r[np.where(np.isnan(kernel_array))], kernel_theta[np.where(np.isnan(kernel_array))])
288            raise ValueError("NaN dose rate values in the TG-43 dose rate kernel.")
289
290        np.clip(kernel_array, a_min = 0.0, a_max = self.calc_parameters["kernel_max_dose_rate"], out=kernel_array)
291        logging.debug("Generating TG-43 dose rate kernel image.")
292        kernel_dose_image = DoseImage(imageArray=kernel_array, name='TG-43 Dose Kernel',
293            origin=(-kernel_half_width,-kernel_half_width,-kernel_half_width), spacing = (kernel_res, kernel_res, kernel_res))
294        self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel = BrachyDose(dtype=np.float16)
295        self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel.dose_image = kernel_dose_image
296        if debug_pth_out is not None:
297            logging.debug("Writing dose rate kernel to path %s", debug_pth_out)
298            self.tg43_dose_rate_kernel.write_brachydose_to_file(debug_pth_out)
299        logging.debug("TG-43 dose rate kernel generation complete.")

  • to run the dose generation for the plan and return a plan with combined dose filled as well as the dose rate dictionary if desired.

  • dir_export := The directory used for exporting the dosimetry setup and the generated dose maps.

  • plan: BrachyPlan := The brachy plan with the combined dose and optionally the dose rate dict filled.
